start_date.description:
The effective date when this contract's compensation terms take effect.

Serves as the anchor point for determining which contract is active — the active contract is the one with the most recent start_date on or before the current date whose end_date is either absent (ongoing) or not yet passed. Modifying this date may shift which contract in the employee's history is considered active, so validation ensures no overlap with adjacent contracts.
start_date.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_contracts.start_date. Changing this may shift which contract is considered active — validation must ensure the new start_date does not cause overlap with adjacent contracts. When updating the active contract's start_date, verify no newer contract exists whose start_date would conflict.

end_date.description:
The date when this contract's compensation terms expire.

When absent (null), the contract is ongoing with no predetermined termination date and remains in effect until superseded by a newer contract or the employee leaves the organization. When present, the contract is effective from start_date through end_date inclusive. Once the end_date passes, the contract becomes a historical record.
end_date.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_contracts.end_date. Nullable — set to null for an ongoing contract with no predetermined termination. When provided, must be chronologically after start_date. A past end_date causes the contract to become historical and immutable.

pay_rate.description:
The numeric amount the employee earns per unit of time as defined by the pay_period.

For example, 25.50 with an hourly pay_period means the employee earns 25.50 currency units per hour worked. The actual currency unit is determined by the organization's settings. Must be greater than zero.
pay_rate.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_contracts.pay_rate. Must be greater than zero (enforced by exclusiveMinimum: 0 in schema). Stored as double-precision float in the database.

pay_period.description:
The unit of time against which the pay_rate is measured.

Determines how the pay rate is applied to calculate compensation. Supported values are hourly (pay_rate applies per hour worked), daily (per full workday), weekly (per full workweek), and monthly (per calendar month). Combined with pay_rate, this defines the complete compensation structure for the contract.
pay_period.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_contracts.pay_period. Must be one of: hourly, daily, weekly, monthly. Used in conjunction with pay_rate to determine the employee's compensation structure. Validation must reject any value outside this set.

working_hours_per_week.description:
The employee's expected weekly time commitment under this contract.

For example, 40 for a standard full-time arrangement, or 37.5 for a slightly reduced schedule. This value informs budget calculations and capacity planning — it is used to compare planned budget hours against actual logged hours in project budget reports and workforce summaries. Must be greater than zero.
working_hours_per_week.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_contracts.working_hours_per_week. Must be greater than zero (enforced by exclusiveMinimum: 0 in schema). Stored as double-precision float. Used for budget calculations and capacity planning across the organization.

notes.description:
Optional free-form notes recording additional details about the compensation agreement.

May include information such as bonus structures, overtime policies, equity grants, or special terms that fall outside the structured fields of pay_rate, pay_period, and working_hours_per_week. This field is purely informational and has no effect on calculations or business logic.
notes.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_contracts.notes. Nullable — free-form text for additional compensation details such as bonus structures, overtime policies, or special terms outside the structured fields. No validation constraints beyond string typing.

IErpHrmContract.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating an employee's currently active contract compensation terms.

All fields are optional — include only the fields you wish to change. The contract to update is identified by the contractId path parameter and must be the employee's active contract. Past contracts that have been superseded by newer agreements or whose end date has passed are preserved as immutable historical records and cannot be modified.

**Editable Fields**

- start_date: The effective date when compensation terms take effect. Modifying this may shift which contract is considered active.
- end_date: The expiration date for the contract term. Set to null to indicate an ongoing contract with no predetermined termination date.
- pay_rate: The numeric compensation amount per unit of time as defined by the pay_period. Must be greater than zero.
- pay_period: The classification of how pay_rate is applied — hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly.
- working_hours_per_week: The expected weekly time commitment under this contract, used for capacity planning and budget calculations.
- notes: Free-form text capturing additional compensation details such as bonus structures, overtime policies, or special terms.

**Constraints**: Only the currently active contract may be edited. System-managed fields such as the contract ID, employee association, and timestamps are not accepted in the request body.
IErpHrmContract.IUpdate.x-autobe-specification: Update DTO for erp_hrm_contracts. All fields are optional — only include fields to change. Maps: start_date → start_date, end_date → end_date (nullable), pay_rate → pay_rate, pay_period → pay_period, working_hours_per_week → working_hours_per_week, notes → notes (nullable). Excluded: id (PK, auto-generated), erp_hrm_employee_id (structural FK — immutable; contract identified by path parameter contractId which resolves the employee), employee (relation — not user-provided in request body), created_at/updated_at/deleted_at (system-managed timestamps). Validation rules: pay_rate > 0, working_hours_per_week > 0, pay_period ∈ {hourly, daily, weekly, monthly}, start_date < end_date when end_date provided, changing start_date must not cause overlap with adjacent contracts. Only the currently active contract (most recent start_date ≤ now with no end_date or end_date ≥ now) can be updated — past contracts are immutable historical records. On update, refresh updated_at and emit contract-edited real-time event.

search.description:
Text search on project name. Supports partial matching via trigram fuzzy search.

Searches the project name column using PostgreSQL trigram similarity. This enables typo-tolerant and partial-string matching, so searching for "market" will find projects named "Marketing", "Market Research", or similar variations.
search.x-autobe-specification: Fuzzy search on erp_hrm_projects.name using the gin_trgm_ops trigram index. Translates to a similarity or ILIKE query (e.g., WHERE name ILIKE '%' || search || '%' or equivalent pg_trgm similarity operator). Supports partial name matching.

status.description:
Filter by project lifecycle status. Accepts 'active', 'archived', or 'completed'. When omitted, returns projects of all statuses.

Projects progress through three lifecycle stages: active projects accept new time entries and task creation; archived projects are preserved but frozen; completed projects have finished and are frozen. Use this filter to narrow results to a specific stage.
status.x-autobe-specification: Exact match filter on erp_hrm_projects.status. Accepts three lifecycle values: 'active' (accepting time entries), 'archived' (frozen, preserved), 'completed' (finished, frozen). When omitted, no status filter is applied and projects of all statuses are returned.

page.description:
Page number for offset-based pagination. 1-indexed (first page is 1).

Controls which page of results to return. Combined with limit to compute the database offset for the SELECT query. The response includes pagination metadata (current page, total pages, total records) for building navigation controls.
page.x-autobe-specification: Pagination control for offset calculation. 1-indexed (first page is 1). Translated to SQL OFFSET as (page - 1) * limit. Must be >= 1. Defaults to 1 when omitted.

limit.description:
Number of projects per page. Maximum 100.

Controls how many project summaries are returned in a single response. The actual number may be fewer on the last page when total records don't divide evenly. Lower values improve response time; higher values reduce the number of requests needed to browse large datasets.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Pagination control for maximum records per page. Translated to SQL LIMIT. Must be between 1 and 100 inclusive. Defaults when omitted.

sort.description:
Sort criteria as an array of [field, direction] pairs. Supported fields: 'name', 'created_at'. Directions: 'ASC', 'DESC'. Example: ['name', 'ASC']. Defaults to ['created_at', 'DESC'] when omitted.

Controls the ordering of returned projects. Multiple sort criteria are applied in array order (e.g., sort by status first, then by name). The default ordering places the most recently created projects at the top of the list.
sort.x-autobe-specification: Multi-field sort specification as an array of [field, direction] pairs. Each pair is processed in order to build the SQL ORDER BY clause. Supported fields: 'name' (sorts on erp_hrm_projects.name), 'created_at' (sorts on erp_hrm_projects.created_at). Supported directions: 'ASC', 'DESC'. Defaults to ['created_at', 'DESC'] when sort is omitted or empty, ensuring newest projects appear first.

IErpHrmProject.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for browsing and filtering projects within the current organization.

Provides search, status filtering, and pagination controls for the project list endpoint. All parameters are optional — when none are specified, the endpoint returns all active, archived, and completed projects (excluding soft-deleted) ordered by newest first.

This is a pure request DTO with no direct database table mapping. It collects query parameters that are translated into SQL WHERE, ORDER BY, LIMIT, and OFFSET clauses against the erp_hrm_projects table.
IErpHrmProject.IRequest.x-autobe-specification:
Query parameters for browsing erp_hrm_projects scoped to session organization (organization_id = session.organization_id).

Filters:
- search: Trigram fuzzy match on the name column using the gin_trgm_ops index. Supports partial name matching via pg_trgm similarity operators.
- status: Exact match on the status column. Accepts 'active', 'archived', or 'completed'. When omitted, returns projects of all statuses.

Always applied: WHERE deleted_at IS NULL (exclude soft-deleted projects).

Pagination: Offset-based using page (1-indexed) and limit. Compute OFFSET as (page - 1) * limit. Maximum 100 records per page.

Sorting: Default ordering by created_at DESC (newest first). When sort parameter is provided, apply specified sort fields in array order. Supported fields: 'name', 'created_at'. Supported directions: 'ASC', 'DESC'.

Authorization: Requires project:view permission. Returns 403 Forbidden otherwise.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the employee record within the organization.

A UUID v4 string that serves as the primary key for all employee operations. This identifier is used in API paths (e.g., /erpHrm/member/employees/{employeeId}) and as a foreign key reference in related entities such as contracts, project memberships, timelogs, and timesheets.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_employees.id. Primary key, UUID format, auto-generated on creation. Used as the unique identifier in all employee-related API paths.

position.description:
The employee's job title or position name within the organization.

Purely descriptive — carries no inherent permissions. Used for organizational clarity, reporting, and display in employee directories. May be null when no position has been assigned to the employee.
position.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_employees.position. Nullable string — no format constraints beyond max length. Free-text job title such as "Software Engineer" or "Marketing Lead".

employment_type.description:
Classification of the employment relationship.

Determines how the employee appears in workforce summaries and organizational charts. Valid values are `full-time`, `part-time`, `contractor`, and `intern`. Used for filtering and reporting across the organization.
employment_type.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_employees.employment_type. Constrained to one of: full-time, part-time, contractor, intern. Always non-null — every employee has an employment type.

status.description:
Current activity status of the employee within the organization.

Controls the employee's ability to perform actions within the platform. `active` employees can log time, submit timesheets, and participate in projects. `deactivated` employees retain all historical data — timelogs, timesheets, contracts, and project memberships — but cannot create new timelogs, edit existing timelogs, or submit timesheets. Deactivation is reversible through the reactivate endpoint.
status.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_employees.status. Constrained to one of: active, deactivated. Always non-null. Status transitions are handled via dedicated endpoints (deactivate/reactivate).

member.description:
The user account profile associated with this employee record.

Contains the member's global identity fields — display name, email, avatar, and phone number — shared across all organizations the member belongs to. Also includes organization-specific employment details such as the employee ID, position, employment type, status, assigned role name, and department name within the current organization. This consolidated view enables callers to display complete employee information without additional API calls.
member.x-autobe-specification: INNER JOIN erp_hrm_members via erp_hrm_member_id. Returns IErpHrmMember.ISummary — a consolidated view combining the member's global profile (id, email, display_name, avatar_image, phone_number) with organization-specific employment details (employee_id, position, employment_type, status, role_name, department_name). INNER JOIN is appropriate because every employee must have a member.

role.description:
The role assigned to this employee, determining their permissions within the organization.

Each employee holds exactly one role at all times. The role's permission set defines all access rights for the employee and takes effect immediately upon assignment. Includes the role's unique identifier, display name, built-in status (indicating whether it is one of the three immutable built-in roles: Owner, Manager, or Employee), optional description, and the count of permissions granted to the role.
role.x-autobe-specification: INNER JOIN erp_hrm_roles via erp_hrm_role_id. Returns IErpHrmRole.ISummary with the role's id, name, is_builtin flag, description, permissions_count, created_at, and updated_at. INNER JOIN — every employee has a role. The role's permission set determines all access rights for the employee.

department.description:
The department this employee belongs to, or null if not assigned to any department.

Department assignment is purely organizational — it carries no inherent permissions and is used for grouping, filtering, and reporting purposes. An employee can exist without a department. When a department is deleted, affected employees have their department reference cleared without removing the employee records themselves.
department.x-autobe-specification: LEFT JOIN erp_hrm_departments via erp_hrm_department_id. Returns IErpHrmDepartment.ISummary when the employee is assigned to a department, null otherwise. Department is optional — erp_hrm_department_id may be null. When a department is deleted, the reference is cleared without affecting the employee record.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the employee record was created.

Set automatically when the employee joins the organization, whether through invitation acceptance or direct assignment. This value is immutable — it is never modified after the initial creation and serves as an audit record of when the employee's membership began.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_employees.created_at. DateTime with timezone (ISO 8601 format). Set automatically when the employee record is created — either through invitation acceptance or direct assignment. Never modified after creation.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent modification to the employee record.

Updated automatically whenever any employee attribute changes, including role reassignment, department placement, position updates, employment type classification changes, and status transitions between active and deactivated. Provides an audit trail of when the employee's organizational identity was last altered.
updated_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_employees.updated_at. DateTime with timezone (ISO 8601 format). Automatically updated on every modification to the employee record, including role reassignment, department changes, position updates, employment type changes, and status transitions.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for data retention and audit integrity.

When set, the employee record is considered removed but preserved for audit purposes. Soft-deleted records are excluded from all query results — this field will always be null in API responses. Set during organization deletion cascades or account deletion cleanup. The timestamp is retained for potential recovery within the data retention window.
deleted_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_employees.deleted_at. Nullable DateTime with timezone. Soft-deleted records (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) are excluded from query results, so this field is always null in API responses. Preserved in the schema for type completeness and to support potential future recovery flows.

IErpHrmEmployee.description:
Complete employee profile within an organization.

Represents a single employee's organizational identity including their unique identifier, assigned role with permissions, optional department placement, position title, employment type classification, and current activity status. The member field provides the user's global profile information — display name, email, avatar, and phone — shared across all organizations they belong to.

This is a Read DTO returned by employee detail endpoints. Deactivated employees are returned with their full historical data intact — deactivation prevents new time tracking and timesheet submission but does not affect record visibility. Soft-deleted employees are excluded from query results.
IErpHrmEmployee.x-autobe-specification: Query erp_hrm_employees by id within the current organization scope (erp_hrm_organization_id = session organization). INNER JOIN erp_hrm_members on erp_hrm_member_id to include the member's display_name, email, avatar_image, and phone_number. INNER JOIN erp_hrm_roles on erp_hrm_role_id to include the role's name, is_builtin flag, description, and permissions_count. LEFT JOIN erp_hrm_departments on erp_hrm_department_id to include the department name and description (null if no department assigned). Exclude soft-deleted records (deleted_at IS NOT NULL). Authorization: require employee:view OR employee:manage permission on the current organization.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the role.

The primary key is a UUID generated by the system when the role is created. For built-in roles, this occurs at organization creation time. For custom roles, this occurs when an owner defines the role.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_roles.id. UUID primary key, system-generated at role creation.

name.description:
Human-readable role name that uniquely identifies the role within its organization.

Serves as the primary way users and administrators distinguish between different roles. Must be unique within a single organization — no two roles in the same organization can share the same name. Examples include the three built-in names (Owner, Manager, Employee) and custom names such as Finance Manager or Senior Developer.
name.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_roles.name. Enforced unique within organization via composite unique constraint [erp_hrm_organization_id, name].

is_builtin.description:
Indicates whether this role is one of the three built-in roles provisioned automatically at organization creation.

Built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) are immutable — they can never be deleted or modified regardless of how many employees are assigned. Custom roles have this flag set to false and may be soft-deleted when no employees are assigned to them.
is_builtin.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_roles.is_builtin. True for the three immutable built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee), false for custom roles.

description.description:
Optional description explaining the role's intended purpose, scope, and responsibilities within the organization.

Provides context for organization owners and administrators when managing roles, clarifying what level of access each role entails. May be null if no description has been set.
description.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_roles.description. Nullable — null when no description has been provided.

permissions.description:
The complete set of permissions granted to members assigned to this role.

Each entry in the array represents a single permission from the system's fixed permission catalog, identified by a unique dot-notation key (e.g., "org:manage", "time:approve") and a human-readable description of the access it grants. The permission set determines all access rights for employees holding this role.

Permission changes take effect immediately — when an owner updates the role's permissions, all employees assigned to the role receive the updated access rights without requiring re-authentication.
permissions.x-autobe-specification: Resolved via rolePermissions has-many relation on erp_hrm_roles → erp_hrm_role_permissions junction table → erp_hrm_permissions. Each junction row carries a permission ID that joins to the permissions catalog. Project each resolved permission to IErpHrmPermission.ISummary (id, key, description). Load eagerly with the role query for complete permission context.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the role was created.

For built-in roles, this matches the organization creation time since they are provisioned automatically. For custom roles, this reflects when the organization owner created the role.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_roles.created_at. Set at role creation — matches organization creation time for built-in roles, reflects owner action time for custom roles.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the role was last modified.

Updated whenever the role's name, description, or permission set changes. Permission changes propagate immediately — the timestamp reflects when the modification was applied, and all employees assigned to the role receive updated access rights from that moment.
updated_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_roles.updated_at. Updated whenever the role's name, description, or permission set changes.

deleted_at.description:
Soft-delete timestamp for the role.

Null for active roles and all built-in roles (which are never deletable). Set to the deletion timestamp when an organization owner soft-deletes a custom role that has no employees assigned to it. Soft-deleted roles are excluded from normal query results but preserved for audit integrity.
deleted_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_roles.deleted_at. Null for active roles and all built-in roles. Set when an owner soft-deletes a custom role with no assigned employees.

IErpHrmRole.description:
A role definition within an organization, including its name, description, built-in status, and the complete set of permissions granted to members assigned to this role.

Roles form the foundation of the role-based access control system. Each employee in an organization holds exactly one role, and the role's permission set determines all access rights for that employee. The three built-in roles — Owner, Manager, and Employee — are provisioned automatically at organization creation and are immutable. Custom roles can be created, updated, and soft-deleted by organization owners.

The permissions array contains the full set of permissions currently assigned to the role, each represented as a summary with its unique key and human-readable description. Permission changes propagate immediately — any employee assigned to this role will have their effective access rights updated instantly when the permission set changes.

The is_builtin flag identifies roles that cannot be modified or deleted. Built-in roles always have this flag set to true. The deleted_at timestamp indicates when a custom role was soft-deleted; it is always null for active roles and built-in roles.
IErpHrmRole.x-autobe-specification: Read DTO for erp_hrm_roles table. Direct column mappings: id, name, is_builtin, description, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at. The permissions array is resolved via the rolePermissions has-many relation through the erp_hrm_role_permissions junction table to erp_hrm_permissions, with each entry projected to IErpHrmPermission.ISummary (id, key, description). Organization scoping: erp_hrm_organization_id filtered server-side by session's selected organization context — never exposed in the response payload. Soft-deleted records (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) excluded at query level — the DTO's deleted_at field shows null for active roles and the deletion timestamp for soft-deleted roles.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the member account.

A UUID that uniquely identifies this member across the entire platform. This identifier is assigned at account creation and remains immutable throughout the account's lifetime.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_members.id. UUID primary key assigned at account creation. Immutable.

email.description:
The member's email address used for authentication and as the primary contact identifier.

Must be unique across all member accounts. Used during login for credential matching and during sign-up to check for existing accounts. Also serves as the target for organization invitations — when an invitation is sent to an email matching an existing member, the member is automatically added to the inviting organization.
email.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_members.email. Enforced unique across all member accounts by database constraint.

display_name.description:
The member's visible display name shown across the platform.

Part of the global profile shared across all organizations the member belongs to. Displayed in employee lists, project member views, task assignments, activity logs, and all other contexts where the member's identity is shown. Changes to this field take effect immediately across all organizations.
display_name.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_members.display_name. Not-null string. Must not be empty or whitespace-only when updated via profile update endpoint.

avatar_image.description:
URI pointing to the member's avatar image for visual identification.

Part of the global profile. When set, this image is displayed alongside the member's name throughout the platform. A null value indicates the member has not set an avatar, and a default placeholder should be displayed instead.
avatar_image.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_members.avatar_image. Nullable VarChar(80000). When set, must be a valid URI. Null indicates no avatar — use a default placeholder.

phone_number.description:
The member's contact phone number.

Part of the global profile. Stored as a free-text string to accommodate international number formats. A null value indicates the member has not provided a phone number.
phone_number.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_members.phone_number. Nullable. Free-text string to accommodate international number formats.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the member account was created.

Records the date and time when the member completed the sign-up process and their account was established. This timestamp is immutable and set automatically by the system at account creation.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_members.created_at. Timestamptz. Set automatically at account creation and immutable.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent modification to the member's account or profile.

Updated automatically whenever any field of the member record is modified, including profile updates (display name, avatar, phone number) and account status changes. Provides visibility into when the profile was last changed.
updated_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_members.updated_at. Timestamptz. Automatically updated on every modification to the member record.

IErpHrmMember.description:
Full member profile containing the global profile fields and account metadata.

The profile includes the member's unique identifier, email address, display name, avatar image URI, and phone number — collectively forming the global profile that is shared across all organizations the member belongs to. Account creation and last update timestamps are also included.

Sensitive authentication data such as password hashes is never exposed through this schema. Members whose accounts have been soft-deleted are treated as not found and are not returned.
IErpHrmMember.x-autobe-specification:
Query the erp_hrm_members table by member ID. Select and return the following columns only: id, email, display_name, avatar_image, phone_number, created_at, updated_at.

Never include password_hash in the response under any circumstances. Members with deleted_at set (non-null) must be filtered out at the service layer — deleted accounts return 404 Not Found.

Verify the requesting user is authenticated as a member and shares an organization with the target member. The target member must have at least one active employee record (erp_hrm_employees.status = 'active') in the requesting user's currently selected organization. If no such employee record exists, return 403 Forbidden. No organization context on session → 401 Unauthorized.

search.description:
Free-text search query for finding sessions by member identity.

Matches against the member's display name and email address using case-insensitive partial matching. Useful for quickly locating a specific member's sessions without knowing their exact member ID.
search.x-autobe-specification: ILIKE text search on erp_hrm_members.display_name OR erp_hrm_members.email, executed via JOIN erp_hrm_members ON sessions.erp_hrm_member_id = members.id. Leverages the GIN trigram index on display_name for efficient prefix and partial matching. The search term is matched against both the member's display name and email address simultaneously using case-insensitive pattern matching.

member_ids.description:
Filter sessions by one or more specific member identifiers.

Accepts an array of member UUIDs to retrieve sessions belonging to those members only. When multiple IDs are provided, sessions matching any of the specified members are returned. All IDs are automatically scoped to the current organization.
member_ids.x-autobe-specification: IN filter on erp_hrm_member_sessions.erp_hrm_member_id column. Accepts an array of UUIDs for multi-select filtering. Each UUID must reference a valid member in erp_hrm_members. Results are scoped to sessions belonging to any of the specified members. The target database column is erp_hrm_member_id on the erp_hrm_member_sessions table.

created_at_start.description:
Filter sessions created on or after this timestamp.

Defines the inclusive lower bound of the session creation date range. Sessions with a creation time equal to or later than this value are included. Must be a valid ISO 8601 datetime string such as "2026-01-15T00:00:00Z".
created_at_start.x-autobe-specification: Lower bound range filter on erp_hrm_member_sessions.created_at column. Inclusive comparison (>=). Must be a valid ISO 8601 datetime string. Sessions created at or after this timestamp are included. When combined with created_at_end, defines a closed-open interval. The target database column is created_at on the erp_hrm_member_sessions table.

created_at_end.description:
Filter sessions created before this timestamp.

Defines the exclusive upper bound of the session creation date range. Sessions created before this value are included, while sessions created at or after are excluded. Must be a valid ISO 8601 datetime string such as "2026-01-31T23:59:59Z".
created_at_end.x-autobe-specification: Upper bound range filter on erp_hrm_member_sessions.created_at column. Exclusive comparison (<). Must be a valid ISO 8601 datetime string. Sessions created before this timestamp are included. When combined with created_at_start, defines a closed-open interval. The target database column is created_at on the erp_hrm_member_sessions table.

status.description:
Filter sessions by their current status.

Determines whether a session is still valid or has expired based on its expiration timestamp relative to the current time. Active sessions have not yet reached their expiration time and can still be used for API requests. Expired sessions have passed their expiration time and require re-authentication.
status.x-autobe-specification: Derived filter computed from erp_hrm_member_sessions.expired_at column compared against the current server timestamp (NOW()). 'active' maps to WHERE expired_at > NOW() — sessions that have not yet reached expiration. 'expired' maps to WHERE expired_at <= NOW() — sessions past their expiration time. No direct column equality; the filter value is computed at query time from the expired_at column.

page.description:
Page number for offset-based pagination.

Specifies which page of results to return. Page numbering starts at 1 for the first page. Combined with `limit`, this controls the window of records returned in the response. When omitted, the first page is returned by default.
page.x-autobe-specification: 1-based page number for offset-based pagination. Translated to SQL offset as (page - 1) * limit. Default is 1 when not provided. Must be a positive integer. When page exceeds available pages, an empty result set is returned.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records to return per page.

Controls the page size for offset-based pagination. Accepts values from 1 to 100, with a default of 20 when not specified. Smaller values reduce payload size and improve response times; larger values reduce the number of requests needed to browse the full result set.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Maximum number of records per page for offset-based pagination. Must be an integer between 1 and 100 inclusive. Default is 20 when not provided. Maps to SQL LIMIT clause. The actual number of returned records may be less on the final page.

IErpHrmMemberSession.IRequest.description:
Search criteria for browsing member sessions within the current organization.

Supports filtering by member identity via text search or member ID list, session creation date range, and session status (active or expired). All fields are optional — an empty request body returns all sessions scoped to the current organization with default pagination of 20 records per page, ordered newest first.

Pagination uses offset-based navigation: `page` starts at 1, `limit` ranges from 1 to 100 with a default of 20. The `status` filter compares the session expiration timestamp against the current time to determine whether a session is still active or has expired.
IErpHrmMemberSession.IRequest.x-autobe-specification:
Query filter DTO for browsing erp_hrm_member_sessions scoped to the current organization via server-side JOIN with erp_hrm_employees.

search: ILIKE on erp_hrm_members.display_name OR erp_hrm_members.email through JOIN erp_hrm_members ON sessions.erp_hrm_member_id = members.id. Leverages the GIN trigram index on display_name for efficient prefix and partial matching.

member_ids: IN filter on erp_hrm_member_sessions.erp_hrm_member_id. Array enables multi-select filtering by UUID.

created_at_start/created_at_end: Range filter on erp_hrm_member_sessions.created_at. created_at_start is inclusive (>=), created_at_end is exclusive (<). Both must be valid ISO 8601 datetime strings.

status: Derived filter — 'active' maps to WHERE expired_at > NOW(), 'expired' maps to WHERE expired_at <= NOW(). Compares erp_hrm_member_sessions.expired_at against current timestamp.

page: 1-based page number for offset pagination. offset = (page - 1) * limit.
limit: Records per page, minimum 1, maximum 100. Default is 20.

Server-side org scoping: JOIN erp_hrm_employees ON sessions.erp_hrm_member_id = employees.erp_hrm_user_id WHERE employees.erp_hrm_organization_id = :currentOrgId. ORDER BY sessions.created_at DESC. Exclude access_token and refresh_token from all response variants.

search.description:
Partial match search on the email address.

Filters verification records whose email address contains the provided search string. Performs case-insensitive substring matching across the full email value, allowing partial inputs like searching for a domain name or name fragment.
search.x-autobe-specification: Partial match filter on erp_hrm_member_email_verifications.email column. Applied as WHERE email ILIKE '%value%' (case-insensitive substring search). No exact matching — any record whose email contains the search string is included.

member_id.description:
Filter by the member account ID.

Restricts results to verification records belonging to a specific member account. The value must be a valid UUID referencing an existing member within the current organization. Useful for auditing a single member's verification history.
member_id.x-autobe-specification: Exact match filter on erp_hrm_member_email_verifications.erp_hrm_member_id column. Applied as WHERE erp_hrm_member_id = value. Value must be a valid UUID. Combined with organization scoping JOIN to ensure the member belongs to the current organization.

oneOf.description: Filter by verification status.
Filter by verification status.
Filter by verification status.

status.description:
Filter by verification status.

Pending tokens have been issued but not yet confirmed — the user still needs to click the verification link before the token expires. Verified tokens have been successfully consumed and the email address is confirmed. Expired tokens exceeded their validity window without being used and are no longer actionable.
status.x-autobe-specification:
Derived filter computed at query time from two columns:
- pending: WHERE verified_at IS NULL AND expires_at > NOW() — token is unverified and still valid.
- verified: WHERE verified_at IS NOT NULL — token was successfully consumed.
- expired: WHERE verified_at IS NULL AND expires_at <= NOW() — token timed out without being used.

Only one status value can be applied per query. The WHERE clause is constructed dynamically based on the selected const value.

created_at_from.description:
Filter records created on or after this timestamp.

Returns verification records whose creation date falls at or later than the specified ISO 8601 datetime. Use together with created_at_to to define a bounded date range. Useful for auditing verification activity within a specific time window.
created_at_from.x-autobe-specification: Inclusive lower bound for date range filter on erp_hrm_member_email_verifications.created_at column. Applied as WHERE created_at >= value. Combined with created_at_to to form a bounded temporal range. Value must be a valid ISO 8601 datetime string.

created_at_to.description:
Filter records created on or before this timestamp.

Returns verification records whose creation date falls at or earlier than the specified ISO 8601 datetime. Use together with created_at_from to define a bounded date range. Useful for auditing verification activity within a specific time window.
created_at_to.x-autobe-specification: Inclusive upper bound for date range filter on erp_hrm_member_email_verifications.created_at column. Applied as WHERE created_at <= value. Combined with created_at_from to form a bounded temporal range. Value must be a valid ISO 8601 datetime string.

sort_field.description:
Field to sort results by.

Controls which column determines the ordering of returned records. Available options include creation date (default), email address, expiration date, and verification date. Sorting by email is useful for alphabetical browsing; sorting by expires_at helps identify tokens nearing expiration.
sort_field.x-autobe-specification:
Controls the ORDER BY clause column in the SQL query. Maps to erp_hrm_member_email_verifications columns:
- created_at: sort by token issuance timestamp (default).
- email: sort by the email address alphabetically.
- expires_at: sort by token expiration timestamp.
- verified_at: sort by verification completion timestamp (nulls sort according to database defaults).

Defaults to created_at when the property is not provided.

oneOf.description: Sort direction. Defaults to desc.
Sort direction. Defaults to desc.

sort_direction.description:
Sort direction for the result set.

Ascending order returns records from earliest to latest or alphabetically A to Z. Descending order returns records from latest to earliest or alphabetically Z to A. Defaults to descending, placing the most recent verification records at the top of the first page.
sort_direction.x-autobe-specification:
Sort direction for the ORDER BY clause:
- asc: ascending — A→Z for email, oldest→newest for timestamps.
- desc: descending — Z→A for email, newest→oldest for timestamps (default).

Defaults to desc when the property is not provided, showing most recent records first.

next.description:
Cursor token for pagination.

An opaque string returned from a previous page of results that identifies the exact position to continue from. Providing this token retrieves the next page of records without skipping or duplicating entries. Omit for the first page. Cursor-based pagination ensures stable ordering even when new records are inserted between page requests.
next.x-autobe-specification:
Opaque cursor token enabling cursor-based pagination. Returned in the pagination metadata of a previous page response. Encodes the last record's sort field values (determined by sort_field) to set the starting point for the next page query. Applied as WHERE (sort_field, id) > (cursor_sort_value, cursor_id) with appropriate comparison direction based on sort_direction.

Omit or set to null for the first page of results.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records to return per page.

Controls the page size within a valid range of 1 to 100 records. Smaller values reduce payload size and improve response time for quick browsing. Larger values reduce the total number of requests needed to traverse the full result set. The actual returned count may be fewer on the final page.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Page size controlling the maximum number of records returned per page. Applied as LIMIT in the SQL query. Constrained to range 1–100 inclusive. Defaults to a system-defined value (typically 20) when not provided.

page.description:
Target page number to retrieve.

Specifies which page of results to return using 1-based indexing, where the first page is page 1. When omitted, null, or undefined, the first page is returned by default. Requesting a page number beyond the available range returns an empty data array with accurate pagination metadata. This field is ignored when a cursor token is provided via the next parameter, as cursor-based navigation takes precedence.
page.x-autobe-specification:
1-indexed target page number. Defaults to 1 when omitted, null, or undefined. Translated to OFFSET in the SQL query: OFFSET = (page - 1) * limit. Page numbering starts from 1, so page 1 returns rows 0 through limit-1. Requesting a page beyond the available range (page > ceiling(records / limit)) returns an empty data array with valid pagination metadata reflecting actual totals.

When used together with next cursor, page is ignored in favor of cursor-based navigation.

IErpHrmMemberEmailVerification.IRequest.description:
Search and pagination parameters for listing email verification records.

Provides filtering, sorting, and pagination controls for browsing member email verification tokens within the current organization. Verification tokens are issued automatically during the sign-up flow and track whether a member's email address is pending confirmation, successfully verified, or expired.

Results are automatically scoped to the active organization through a join on the member account and employee record. Only verification records belonging to members who are employees of the current organization are returned. Deleted member accounts are excluded from results.
IErpHrmMemberEmailVerification.IRequest.x-autobe-specification:
Query parameter object for filtering erp_hrm_member_email_verifications records. Not a direct table mapping — each property controls a different aspect of the SQL query:

search: WHERE email ILIKE '%value%' (case-insensitive substring match on erp_hrm_member_email_verifications.email).
member_id: WHERE erp_hrm_member_id = value (exact UUID match).
status: Derived WHERE clause — pending: verified_at IS NULL AND expires_at > NOW(); verified: verified_at IS NOT NULL; expired: verified_at IS NULL AND expires_at <= NOW().
created_at_from: WHERE created_at >= value (inclusive lower bound).
created_at_to: WHERE created_at <= value (inclusive upper bound).
sort_field: ORDER BY column — valid values: created_at, email, expires_at, verified_at. Defaults to created_at.
sort_direction: ORDER BY direction — asc or desc. Defaults to desc.
next: Opaque cursor token for cursor-based pagination, encoding the last row's sort field values.
limit: LIMIT clause — page size, range 1–100.
page: OFFSET computed as (page - 1) * limit. 1-indexed, defaults to 1.

Data Isolation: All queries must JOIN erp_hrm_member_id → erp_hrm_members → erp_hrm_employees to scope results to the current organization context. Exclude records where the member has been deleted (erp_hrm_members.deleted_at IS NOT NULL).

id.description:
Unique identifier for the department.

A UUID v4 primary key generated automatically when the department is created. This identifier is globally unique and used as the target for parent_id references in the self-referencing department hierarchy.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_departments.id. UUID primary key, auto-generated on creation.

name.description:
The department's display name.

Must be unique within the organization — no two departments in the same organization can share the same name. Used for display in department listings, employee records, and organizational hierarchy views. This uniqueness constraint is enforced across all non-deleted departments.
name.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_departments.name. Must be unique within the organization (enforced by @@unique([erp_hrm_organization_id, name])). Non-empty string.

description.description:
Optional free-text description of the department's purpose or scope.

Provides additional context for employees browsing the organizational structure. May be null when no description has been set, or an empty string when the description was cleared. This field is updated independently of the department name.
description.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_departments.description. Nullable — null when no description is provided.

parent.description:
The parent department in the organizational hierarchy.

When set, this references the department directly above this one in the hierarchy, forming a one-level nesting structure. The referenced parent department is a top-level department — it cannot itself have a parent, enforcing the constraint that only two levels of nesting are permitted.

For top-level departments, this field is null, indicating the department sits at the root of its hierarchy branch. Use this field to reconstruct the department tree for navigation and breadcrumb display.
parent.x-autobe-specification: BELONGS-TO self-referencing relation resolved via parent_id JOIN to erp_hrm_departments. Returns IErpHrmDepartment.ISummary for the parent department, or null for top-level departments. The one-level nesting constraint ensures a parent department cannot itself have a parent.

erp_hrm_organization_id.description:
The organization this department belongs to.

Each department is strictly scoped to a single organization as part of the multi-tenancy data isolation model. All department operations — including queries, updates, and hierarchy traversal — are bounded by the currently selected organization context. This value is set automatically from the authenticated session when the department is created and is never modified.
erp_hrm_organization_id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_departments.erp_hrm_organization_id. Identifies the organization this department belongs to. Set from session context on creation and never changed. Enforces multi-tenancy data isolation.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the department was created.

Set automatically at the moment of creation and remains immutable for the lifetime of the department record. Stored in UTC with timezone awareness. Use this for auditing when the department was first established in the organizational structure.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_departments.created_at. Timestamptz — set automatically on creation and never modified thereafter.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent modification to the department record.

Updated automatically whenever the department's name, description, or parent relationship is changed. Stored in UTC with timezone awareness. Compare with created_at to determine if the department has been modified since its initial creation.
updated_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_departments.updated_at. Timestamptz — updated automatically whenever the department's name, description, or parent relationship changes.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for data retention and recovery.

When null, the department is active and visible in all standard queries. When set, the department has been soft-deleted — its record is preserved for audit and potential recovery, but it is excluded from normal listing and retrieval operations. A department with active child departments cannot be soft-deleted until all children are reassigned or deleted first.
deleted_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_departments.deleted_at. Nullable Timestamptz — null for active departments, set to the deletion timestamp for soft-deleted departments. Query logic must filter out soft-deleted records (WHERE deleted_at IS NULL) unless explicitly requested.

IErpHrmDepartment.description:
Full department record within an organization.

Departments are organizational groupings that categorize employees by functional area or team — such as Engineering, Sales, or Human Resources. They serve purely as a structural organization tool with no bearing on permissions, access control, or project assignments.

The department hierarchy supports a one-level parent-child nesting pattern: a department may optionally reference a parent department, and a department may serve as a parent to child departments, but a child department cannot itself be a parent. The parent field contains the parent department summary when nested within a hierarchy, and is null for top-level departments.

Soft-deleted departments are indicated by a non-null deleted_at timestamp. All employees within the organization can view any department regardless of their role.
IErpHrmDepartment.x-autobe-specification: Read DTO for the erp_hrm_departments table. Maps all scalar columns directly: id, name, description, erp_hrm_organization_id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at. The parent relation is resolved via a self-referencing BELONGS-TO JOIN on parent_id → IErpHrmDepartment.ISummary, returning null for top-level departments. The parent_id FK column is excluded from the DTO — it exists only as the join key behind the parent $ref object. HAS-MANY relations (children[], employees[]) are excluded: children are retrieved via a separate listing endpoint, and employees are managed through the employee API. Soft-deleted records are identifiable by a non-null deleted_at timestamp; query logic must filter these out unless explicitly requested.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the project membership record.

A UUID v4 value assigned at creation when an employee is first added to a project. This identifier is stable for the lifetime of the membership and is used to reference the specific member-project relationship in subsequent operations such as role updates or member removal.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_project_members.id. UUID primary key.

role.description:
The member's role within the project.

Determines the member's authority level inside the project. A value of "member" indicates a regular participant who can track time and view assigned tasks. A value of "project-lead" grants elevated permissions including the ability to create, edit, assign, and manage tasks within the project. The role can be changed at any time by users with project management permissions, and the new permissions take effect immediately.
role.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_project_members.role. Constrained to "member" or "project-lead".

joined_at.description:
Timestamp recording when the employee was assigned to the project.

Set once at creation time and never modified. This value serves as a permanent audit record of when the membership relationship began, regardless of any subsequent role changes or eventual removal from the project.
joined_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_project_members.joined_at. Immutable — set at creation and never updated.

employee.description:
The employee assigned to the project.

Contains the employee's organizational profile including their member identity (display name, email, avatar), assigned role within the organization, optional department membership, position title, employment type classification, and current active or deactivated status. This is a summary view optimized for list display — use the employee detail endpoint to retrieve the full profile including contracts and project assignments.
employee.x-autobe-specification: Relationship mapping: JOIN erp_hrm_project_members.erp_hrm_employee_id → erp_hrm_employees.id → erp_hrm_members.id. Returns IErpHrmEmployee.ISummary.

IErpHrmProjectMember.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a project member for list display and management views.

The membership includes the employee's assigned role within the project and the immutable joined timestamp recording when the assignment began. The role is either "member" for regular participants or "project-lead" for those with elevated task management authority.

The employee profile provides the member's organizational identity: display name, position title, employment type classification, and current active or deactivated status within the organization.
IErpHrmProjectMember.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Direct: id, role, joined_at. Relations: employee via JOIN on erp_hrm_employee_id → erp_hrm_employees → erp_hrm_members (BELONGS-TO). Excluded: created_at, updated_at (system-managed audit timestamps unnecessary for summary views), deleted_at (soft-delete marker filtered at query level — deleted members are never returned), erp_hrm_employee_id (FK resolved via employee $ref object), erp_hrm_project_id (path context — this ISummary is always scoped to a project endpoint), project (parent project known from URL path context, including it would be redundant).

id.description:
Primary key uniquely identifying the member account across all organizations.

This UUID is the stable identifier for the member throughout the platform. It is used as the subject claim in JWT access tokens, as the foreign key in employee records linking members to organizations, and as the owner reference in all member-owned entities such as timelogs, timesheets, and timers. The id is assigned at account creation and never changes.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_members.id column. Primary key UUID (@db.Uuid) uniquely identifying the member account across all organizations. Used as the subject claim in JWT access tokens and as the foreign key reference in employee records (erp_hrm_employees.erp_hrm_member_id), session records (erp_hrm_member_sessions.erp_hrm_member_id), and all member-owned entities. Non-nullable, always present in all response contexts (join, login, refresh).

email.description:
The member's email address used for authentication and as the primary contact identifier.

Must be unique across all member accounts. Used during login for credential matching and during sign-up to check for existing accounts. Also serves as the target for organization invitations — when an invitation is sent to an email matching an existing member, the member is automatically added to the inviting organization upon email verification.
email.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_members.email column. Enforced as unique across all non-deleted member accounts via @@unique([email]) index. Used as the primary contact identifier and authentication credential (matched against user input during login). Also serves as the matching target for organization invitations — when an invitation is sent to an email matching an existing member, the member is automatically added to the inviting organization upon email verification. Format: email, non-nullable in DB. Always present in every response context.

display_name.description:
The member's visible name displayed across the platform in all organizations they belong to.

Part of the global profile that is shared across all organizations. Displayed in employee lists, project member views, task assignments, activity logs, and all other contexts where the member's identity is shown. This value is set during registration and can be updated through the profile update operation.
display_name.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_members.display_name column. Part of the global profile shared across all organizations the member belongs to. Displayed in employee lists, project member views, task assignments, activity logs, and all other contexts where the member's identity is shown.

Optional URI pointing to the member's avatar image for visual identification.

On join response: always null (newly registered members have no avatar). On login/refresh: the stored value, or null if never set. Format: uri. Optional contact phone number for the member.

phone_number.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_members.phone_number column. Nullable in DB — null when the member has not provided a phone number. Stored as a free-text string to accommodate international number formats. Part of the global profile. On join response: always null (newly registered members have no phone number). On login/refresh: the stored value, or null if never set.

Records the date and time when the member completed the sign-up process and their account was established. This timestamp is immutable and set automatically by the system at account creation.

Timestamp of the most recent modification to the member's account or profile.
