Automatically updated on every modification to the member record including profile updates and account status changes. Since the parent DTO aggregates from multiple tables (erp_hrm_members, erp_hrm_member_sessions, erp_hrm_employees), databaseSchemaProperty is null and the column origin is documented here.

token.x-autobe-specification: Authorization token comes from the session table.

organizations.description:
List of organizations the authenticated member belongs to through active employee records.

Each entry is a summary representation of an organization where the member holds an employee record that has not been deleted. The member's role and permissions within each organization are determined by the employee record's role assignment.

For newly registered members (join response), this array is empty — the member must be invited to or create an organization. For returning members (login/refresh), the array contains all organizations they belong to. When this array contains multiple organizations, the client should present an organization selection interface before proceeding to organization-scoped operations.
organizations.x-autobe-specification:
Computed via JOIN: SELECT organization.* FROM erp_hrm_employees WHERE employee.erp_hrm_member_id = member.id AND employee.deleted_at IS NULL, then resolve each employee.erp_hrm_organization_id to IErpHrmOrganization.ISummary. Results collected into an array.

Join response: empty array [] — new member has no employee records yet. Login/refresh: populated array containing all organizations where the member holds an active (non-deleted) employee record. If exactly one organization exists, the client may auto-select it. If multiple, the client must present an organization selection interface. The selected organization is then set via PUT /erpHrm/member/sessions/organizations.

IErpHrmMember.IAuthorized.description:
Authentication response containing JWT access and refresh tokens, session expiration, the authenticated member's profile, and a list of organizations the member belongs to.

The access token must be included as a Bearer token in the Authorization header on all subsequent authenticated API requests. The refresh token is used to obtain a new access token when the current one expires, without re-entering credentials.

When the member belongs to multiple organizations, the client should present an organization selection interface — the selected organization context scopes all subsequent requests for data isolation.

For newly registered members (join response), organizations is an empty array and optional profile fields (avatar_image and phone_number) are null. Members can update their profile and join organizations through subsequent operations.
IErpHrmMember.IAuthorized.x-autobe-specification:
Computed response type aggregating erp_hrm_members, erp_hrm_member_sessions, and erp_hrm_employees.

Source tables and contributions:
- erp_hrm_members: id, email, display_name, avatar_image, phone_number — direct column mappings for member identity and global profile.
- erp_hrm_member_sessions: access_token, refresh_token, expired_at — composed into nested IAuthorizationToken via token property.
- erp_hrm_employees: JOIN WHERE employee.erp_hrm_member_id = member.id AND employee.deleted_at IS NULL, resolving each employee.erp_hrm_organization_id to IErpHrmOrganization.ISummary, collected into organizations array.

Context-dependent behavior:
- Join response: avatar_image = null, phone_number = null, organizations = [] (new member has no employee records).
- Login/refresh: all profile fields populated from stored values, organizations from active employee records.

Response-only DTO — never used as request body. token.access must be presented as Bearer token in Authorization header on all subsequent authenticated requests.

IErpHrmTask.IRequest.description:
Search, filter, sort, and pagination criteria for listing tasks within a project.

All properties are optional — when omitted, no corresponding filter is applied. Filters that accept arrays ({@link status}, {@link priority}) support multiple values for OR-based matching within each filter category.

Filtering supports narrowing results by task status, priority level, assigned employee, parent task relationship, and due date range. The {@link search} field performs fuzzy text matching against task titles using trigram indexing. Set {@link parentTaskId} to `null` to retrieve only top-level tasks (those without a parent).

Sorting is controlled by {@link sort} (field to sort by) and {@link order} (direction). When both are omitted, results default to creation date descending.

Pagination uses {@link page} and {@link limit} for offset-based navigation. The response includes total matching count for building UI pagination controls.
IErpHrmTask.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: Maps filter fields to erp_hrm_tasks columns: status, priority, erp_hrm_assigned_employee_id, erp_hrm_parent_task_id (nullable for top-level), due_date range, search on title via trigram index. Sortable by due_date, priority, created_at. Pagination via page/limit.

IErpHrmContract.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new employment contract for an employee.

Specifies the compensation terms including pay rate, pay period, working hours per week, and the effective date range. The employee is identified by the `employeeId` path parameter and must not be included in the request body.

When a new contract is created, the system automatically closes the employee's previous active contract by setting its end date to the day before the new contract's start date, ensuring only one contract is active at any given time while preserving all past contracts as immutable historical records.
IErpHrmContract.ICreate.x-autobe-specification: Maps to erp_hrm_contracts table. Direct fields: start_date, end_date (nullable), pay_rate, pay_period, working_hours_per_week, notes (nullable). Excluded: id (auto-generated UUID), erp_hrm_employee_id (from {employeeId} path parameter), created_at/updated_at (auto-set to current timestamp on insert), deleted_at (always null on creation). Business validation: pay_rate > 0, working_hours_per_week > 0, pay_period must be one of hourly/daily/weekly/monthly, if end_date is provided then start_date < end_date. On creation, the system auto-closes the employee's previous active contract by setting its end_date to the day before start_date.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the task history entry.

A UUID primary key that uniquely identifies this status change record across the system. Automatically generated when a task's status is updated and the corresponding history entry is created. Used for direct retrieval of individual history entries via GET endpoints.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_task_histories.id. UUID primary key, auto-generated by the database on history entry creation.

old_status.description:
The task status before the transition occurred.

One of four workflow statuses: open (work not yet started), in-progress (work actively underway), completed (deliverable finished), or closed (formally finalized). Together with new_status, this captures both the origin and destination of the state change, enabling audit review of the full lifecycle path.

Example: if a task moves from in-progress to completed, old_status is 'in-progress' and new_status is 'completed'.
old_status.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_task_histories.old_status. String enum: open, in-progress, completed, closed. Captured at the moment of status transition — the value before the change was applied.

new_status.description:
The task status after the transition occurred.

One of four workflow statuses: open (work not yet started), in-progress (work actively underway), completed (deliverable finished), or closed (formally finalized). Together with old_status, this captures both the origin and destination of the state change.

Example: if a task moves from in-progress to completed, old_status is 'in-progress' and new_status is 'completed'.
new_status.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_task_histories.new_status. String enum: open, in-progress, completed, closed. Captured at the moment of status transition — the value after the change was applied.

changed_by_member.description:
The member who performed the status change.

Identifies the authenticated user who triggered the status transition. This could be the task's assigned employee updating their own task, a project lead managing tasks within their project, or any user with appropriate project management permissions.

The member object includes their global profile — display name, email, avatar image, and phone number — along with their organization-specific employment details such as position title, employment type, role name, and department name within the current organization context.
changed_by_member.x-autobe-specification: Resolved via JOIN: erp_hrm_task_histories.changed_by_member_id → erp_hrm_members.id, returned as IErpHrmMember.ISummary. Uses the relation name changedByMember (not the FK column name) as this is a Read DTO — the raw foreign key is excluded in favor of the resolved entity.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the status change occurred.

Serves as both the creation time of the history entry and the point-in-time marker for the status transition. History entries for a given task are returned in chronological order (oldest first), providing a timeline view of the task's complete lifecycle.

Format: ISO 8601 date-time string with timezone offset (e.g., '2026-01-15T09:30:00+09:00').
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_task_histories.created_at. Timestamptz column, automatically set at history entry creation. Immutable after creation.

IErpHrmTaskHistory.ISummary.description:
A compact representation of a single task status history entry for list display.

Each entry records one status transition in a task's lifecycle, showing the status before the change (old_status), the status after the change (new_status), which member performed the transition (changed_by_member), and when it occurred (created_at). Status values follow the task workflow: open, in-progress, completed, and closed.

History entries are immutable — they are created automatically by the system when a task's status changes and cannot be modified or deleted after creation. The complete chronological record provides a full audit trail of how each task moved through its workflow states.
IErpHrmTaskHistory.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_task_histories for scalar columns: id, old_status, new_status, created_at. Relation: changedByMember resolved via JOIN on changed_by_member_id → erp_hrm_members, returned as IErpHrmMember.ISummary. Results ordered by created_at ascending. FK column erp_hrm_task_id and relation task are excluded — the parent task identity is provided by the URL path parameter when listing histories under a specific task. FK column changed_by_member_id is excluded — the member identity is exposed through the richer relation object instead.

IErpHrmTask.description:
Full detail representation of a task entity within a project.

Tasks are the fundamental units of work within a project, each following a status workflow from open through in-progress and completed to closed. Tasks can be assigned to a single employee who must be a member of the parent project.

**Task Hierarchy**: Tasks support one level of subtask nesting. A task with a parent is a subtask; child tasks of a parent are exposed via {@link childTasks}. A parent task cannot itself have a parent, enforcing a maximum depth of one.

**Status and Priority**: The {@link status} field tracks the current workflow state (open, in-progress, completed, closed). The {@link priority} field indicates urgency (low, medium, high, urgent). Every status change is recorded in {@link statusHistories} for a complete audit trail.
IErpHrmTask.x-autobe-specification: Direct: id, title, description (nullable), status, priority, estimated_hours (nullable), due_date (nullable), created_at, updated_at, deleted_at (nullable). BELONGS-TO: project via erp_hrm_project_id → IErpHrmProject.ISummary, assignedEmployee via erp_hrm_assigned_employee_id → IErpHrmEmployee.ISummary (nullable), parentTask via erp_hrm_parent_task_id → IErpHrmTask.ISummary (nullable, self-referencing). HAS-MANY: childTasks (recursive erp_hrm_tasks[] via parent_task_id) → IErpHrmTask.ISummary[], statusHistories (erp_hrm_task_histories[]) → IErpHrmTaskHistory.ISummary[].

id.description:
Unique identifier for the contract.

A UUID v4 string that serves as the primary key. Automatically generated by the server when the contract is created and immutable thereafter.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_contracts.id. Primary key, UUID v4, auto-generated on creation.

employee.description:
The employee to whom this contract belongs.

Resolved as a summary view of the employee record including the member's profile (display name, email, avatar), assigned role, optional department membership, position title, employment type classification, and current active/deactivated status. The employee must belong to the currently selected organization context.
employee.x-autobe-specification: BELONGS-TO relation resolved via JOIN on erp_hrm_contracts.erp_hrm_employee_id → erp_hrm_employees.id, returned as IErpHrmEmployee.ISummary. The raw FK column erp_hrm_employee_id is not exposed.

start_date.description:
The date when this contract's compensation terms take effect.

The effective date from which the pay rate, pay period, and working hours commitment apply. When determining the active contract for an employee, the contract with the most recent start_date on or before the current date is considered active, provided its end_date is either absent (ongoing) or not yet passed. Requires ISO 8601 date-time format.
start_date.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_contracts.start_date. Timestamptz stored in UTC. Serves as the anchor point for determining which contract is active — the active contract is the one with the most recent start_date on or before the current date.

end_date.description:
The date when this contract's compensation terms expire.

When null, the contract is ongoing with no predetermined end — it remains in effect until superseded by a newer contract or the employee leaves the organization. When set, the contract is effective from start_date through end_date inclusive. Past contracts whose end_date has passed become immutable historical records. Requires ISO 8601 date-time format when present.
end_date.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_contracts.end_date. Nullable Timestamptz. When null, the contract is ongoing with no predetermined termination date and remains in effect until superseded by a newer contract or the employee leaves the organization.

pay_rate.description:
The numeric amount the employee earns per unit of time as defined by the pay period.

For example, a value of 25.50 with an hourly pay_period means the employee earns 25.50 currency units per hour worked. The currency is determined by the organization's settings. Must be a positive number greater than zero.
pay_rate.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_contracts.pay_rate. Double precision float representing the numeric compensation amount per unit of time as defined by pay_period. Must be greater than zero.

pay_period.description:
The unit of time against which the pay rate is measured.

Allowed values:
- `hourly`: The pay rate applies per hour worked
- `daily`: The pay rate applies per full workday
- `weekly`: The pay rate applies per full workweek
- `monthly`: The pay rate applies per calendar month
pay_period.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_contracts.pay_period. String enum restricted to: hourly, daily, weekly, monthly. Determines the unit of time against which pay_rate is measured.

working_hours_per_week.description:
The employee's expected weekly time commitment under this contract.

For example, 40 for a standard full-time arrangement, or 37.5 for a slightly reduced schedule. This value informs budget calculations and capacity planning across the organization. Must be a positive number greater than zero.
working_hours_per_week.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_contracts.working_hours_per_week. Double precision float. Must be greater than zero. Informs budget calculations and capacity planning.

notes.description:
Optional free-form notes recording additional details about the compensation agreement.

May include information such as bonus structures, overtime policies, or special terms that fall outside the structured fields. Null when no additional context is recorded.
notes.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_contracts.notes. Nullable string. Free-form text for additional compensation details beyond the structured fields.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this contract record was created in the system.

Set automatically by the server at the moment of contract creation. Immutable — never changes after initial creation. Requires ISO 8601 date-time format.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_contracts.created_at. Timestamptz set automatically on creation and never modified thereafter.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent modification to this contract record.

Updated automatically by the server whenever any editable field changes. For active contracts, this reflects the last update time. For past contracts that have been superseded or expired, this timestamp is frozen and will not change — such contracts are immutable historical records. Requires ISO 8601 date-time format.
updated_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_contracts.updated_at. Timestamptz updated automatically whenever the contract record is modified. For past contracts (superseded or expired), this timestamp will not change further.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for contracts that were created in error and removed before being superseded.

When null, the contract is active or preserved as a historical record. When set, the contract is considered deleted but the record is retained for audit integrity. Contracts that have been naturally superseded by a newer contract are preserved as historical records rather than soft-deleted. Requires ISO 8601 date-time format when present.
deleted_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_contracts.deleted_at. Nullable Timestamptz. Soft delete marker — when set, the contract is considered removed but preserved for audit integrity. Only contracts created in error (not superseded) receive this marker.

IErpHrmContract.description:
Full details of an employee employment contract including compensation terms, effective dates, and metadata.

Each contract defines the pay rate, the pay period classification (hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly), the expected working hours per week, and optional free-form notes for additional context such as bonus structures or special terms. Contracts form a historical record over an employee's tenure — an employee may have multiple contracts, with only one active at any given time based on start date recency and end date validity. Past contracts that have been superseded or expired become immutable historical records preserved for auditing and compliance purposes.

The employee reference identifies the organization member to whom this contract belongs, resolved as a summary view including their profile, role, department, and employment status.
IErpHrmContract.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_contracts table. Columns: id, start_date, end_date, pay_rate, pay_period, working_hours_per_week, notes, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at. Relation: employee via BELONGS-TO JOIN on erp_hrm_employee_id → erp_hrm_employees, resolved as IErpHrmEmployee.ISummary. The FK column erp_hrm_employee_id is intentionally excluded — the employee reference is exposed only through the resolved relation object. Soft-deleted records (deleted_at not null) should be filtered at query level. Organization context enforced through the employee's organization linkage.

IErpHrmProjectMember.ICreate.description:
Request body for assigning an employee to a project.

Carries the employee to assign and an optional membership role. The target project is specified in the URL path, and the organization context is determined by the authenticated user's session.

The role determines the employee's authority within the project: `member` for regular participants who can track time and view assigned tasks, or `project-lead` for members with task management authority. When omitted, the role defaults to `member`.
IErpHrmProjectMember.ICreate.x-autobe-specification: Maps: erp_hrm_employee_id, role. Excluded: id (auto-generated UUID), erp_hrm_project_id (path parameter), joined_at (system-set immutable), created_at, updated_at, deleted_at (system-managed). Role defaults to 'member' server-side if omitted. Validate role is either 'member' or 'project-lead'.

week_start_date.description:
The Monday date marking the start of the timesheet's calendar week.

Must be a Monday. The system computes the corresponding Sunday as the week end date automatically. Combined with the authenticated employee's identity, this enforces the unique constraint of at most one timesheet per employee per calendar week.

The date determines which ungrouped timelogs are automatically associated with the new timesheet — all timelogs belonging to the employee with dates falling between this Monday and the following Sunday (inclusive) are linked to the timesheet upon creation.
week_start_date.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timesheets.week_start_date. Must be validated as a Monday — reject with 400 if not. Combined with the authenticated employee_id to enforce the unique constraint (one timesheet per employee per week). The server computes week_end_date as this value + 6 days.

IErpHrmTimesheet.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a draft timesheet.

The authenticated employee's timesheet is created for the calendar week starting on the given Monday date. The system automatically computes the week end date as the following Sunday and associates all ungrouped timelogs within that range with the new timesheet.

The timesheet begins in draft status, allowing the employee to add or remove timelogs before submission. Each employee may have at most one timesheet per calendar week.

Future weeks are allowed for draft creation; submission restrictions for future weeks are enforced separately at submission time.
IErpHrmTimesheet.ICreate.x-autobe-specification: Maps: week_start_date directly from request body. Excluded: employee_id (resolved from JWT session's currently selected organization context — the authenticated employee owns the timesheet), status (auto-set to 'draft' on creation), week_end_date (computed as week_start_date + 6 days), reviewed_by_user_id/submitted_at/reviewed_at/rejection_reason (all null on creation — populated during submission and review workflows), id/created_at/updated_at/deleted_at (system-managed — auto-generated on insert). Validate week_start_date falls on a Monday before creating. Check unique constraint on (employee_id, week_start_date) — reject with 409 if duplicate. After insert, auto-associate ungrouped timelogs (employee_id matches, timesheet_id IS NULL, date within week range, deleted_at IS NULL). Deactivated employees must be rejected.

IErpHrmTask.ICreate.description:
Payload for creating a new task within a project.

Tasks are the fundamental work units within a project, each with a title, optional description, workflow status, priority level, estimated hours, and deadline. Tasks support optional assignment to an employee who must be an active member of the project, and one-level subtask nesting through an optional parent task reference that must belong to the same project.

When status is omitted, the task is created in the `open` state. When priority is omitted, it defaults to `medium`. Every status change during the task's lifecycle is automatically recorded in the task's history for a complete audit trail.
IErpHrmTask.ICreate.x-autobe-specification: Maps: title, description, status, priority, estimated_hours, due_date. References: assigned_employee_id (FK to erp_hrm_employees, must be active project member), parent_task_id (self-FK to erp_hrm_tasks, must belong to same project and not itself be a subtask). Excluded: id (auto UUID), erp_hrm_project_id (path param), created_at/updated_at/deleted_at (auto timestamps). Defaults applied by service layer: status='open', priority='medium' when omitted. Validation rules: title non-empty, estimated_hours positive, due_date in future, assigned_employee_id must be active project member, parent_task_id max depth of one.

IErpHrmProject.ICreate.description:
Payload for creating a new project within the currently selected organization.

A project requires a display name and a color code for visual identification in the user interface. The name appears in project lists, timelog entry forms, timesheet summaries, and reports. The color code must be a valid hex color value such as `#FF5733`.

Optional fields provide additional context: a description explaining the project's purpose or scope, budget hours for comparing planned effort against actual logged time in budget reports, and start and end dates to define the project timeline. The project is automatically created in active status, meaning it accepts new timelogs from the moment it is created.
IErpHrmProject.ICreate.x-autobe-specification: Maps directly to erp_hrm_projects. Required: name (non-empty string), color_code (valid hex color, pattern ^#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}$). Optional: description (string, omit for null), budget_hours (number > 0 when provided, omit for null), start_date (datetime, omit for null), end_date (datetime, omit for null). Auto-set by server: id (UUID), organization_id (session), status ('active'), created_at/updated_at (now), deleted_at (null). Validate hex color format and positive budget_hours. Emit project creation real-time event on success.

Automatically set at creation time and never modified thereafter. Used for chronological listing and audit purposes. Represented as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC.

IErpHrmTask.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a task for use in project task boards and paginated list views.

Includes core task attributes — title, status, priority, due date, estimated hours, and creation date — sufficient for browsing and filtering without loading the full task detail. The assignedEmployee field provides the assignee's summary profile when a task is assigned, and is null for unassigned tasks.

For subtasks, the parentTask field contains a summary of the immediate parent task, providing hierarchical context. Top-level tasks have a null parent task. Large fields such as description and composition collections (child tasks, status histories, timelogs) are excluded to keep the payload compact for list rendering. This schema is always queried within the context of a specific project identified by the URL path.
IErpHrmTask.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Direct: id, title, status, priority, estimated_hours, due_date, created_at. Relations: assignedEmployee via JOIN on erp_hrm_assigned_employee_id → IErpHrmEmployee.ISummary (BELONGS-TO, nullable when unassigned), parentTask via self-referencing JOIN on erp_hrm_parent_task_id → IErpHrmTask.ISummary (BELONGS-TO, nullable for top-level tasks). Excluded: description (large text field), erp_hrm_project_id (project context from URL path), updated_at (not needed for list display), deleted_at (soft-delete filtered at query level). HAS-MANY compositions (childTasks, statusHistories, timelogs, timers) excluded per ISummary convention — summarized data loaded via separate endpoints. BELONGS-TO project relation excluded — project identity is already known from the request path.

week_start_date.description:
The Monday date marking the start of the timesheet's calendar week.

Combined with week_end_date, this defines the Monday-to-Sunday range that determines which timelogs are eligible for inclusion in the timesheet. Must be a Monday. When provided without week_end_date, the end date is automatically calculated as 6 days later.
week_start_date.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timesheets.week_start_date. Must be a Monday (ISO day-of-week = 1). When provided alone, week_end_date is auto-derived as week_start_date + 6 days (Sunday). The (employee_id, week_start_date) pair must be unique across all non-deleted timesheets for the same employee.

week_end_date.description:
The Sunday date marking the end of the timesheet's calendar week.

Always exactly 6 days after week_start_date. Must be a Sunday. When provided without week_start_date, the start date is automatically calculated as 6 days earlier.
week_end_date.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timesheets.week_end_date. Must be a Sunday exactly 6 days after week_start_date. When provided alone, week_start_date is auto-derived as week_end_date - 6 days (Monday). The (employee_id, auto-derived week_start_date) pair must be unique across all non-deleted timesheets for the same employee.

IErpHrmTimesheet.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating a draft timesheet's calendar week range.

Each timesheet groups an employee's timelogs for a specific Monday-to-Sunday calendar week. This payload allows the owning employee or a user with the time:manage permission to adjust the week boundaries of a timesheet while it remains in draft status — before submission locks the definition.

Both week_start_date and week_end_date are optional. Provide both to set the week explicitly, provide just one to have the other derived automatically (Monday-to-Sunday, 6-day span), or provide neither for a no-op update. The week range must not overlap with any other timesheet belonging to the same employee.
IErpHrmTimesheet.IUpdate.x-autobe-specification: Mutates: week_start_date, week_end_date in the erp_hrm_timesheets table. Both fields are optional — an empty body is a no-op, providing a single field auto-derives the other (6-day span: week_end_date = week_start_date + 6 days, or week_start_date = week_end_date - 6 days). Only valid when the timesheet is in 'draft' status. Validation (enforced at service layer): week_start_date must be a Monday (ISO day-of-week = 1), week_end_date must be a Sunday exactly 6 days after week_start_date, and the (employee_id, week_start_date) pair must not conflict with any other non-deleted timesheet owned by the same employee (enforcing @@unique([employee_id, week_start_date])). Employee context is resolved from the authenticated session — the employee owning the timesheet cannot be changed through this operation. If any contained timelogs have dates outside the new week range, they remain associated to the timesheet; the caller is responsible for managing timelog membership separately.
