Non-billable timelogs are excluded from those calculations but still count toward total hours worked. This flag is typically set to true by default for new timelogs and can be toggled during updates to correct classification errors.
billable.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timelogs.billable. Boolean flag distinguishing billable from non-billable work. Defaults to true for new timelogs. Used by time reports and project budget reports to separate billable and non-billable hour calculations.

IErpHrmTimelog.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating an existing timelog entry.

Allows modifying the core details of a previously logged time entry: the date work was performed, the duration in minutes, the target project, an optional task within that project, a free-text description of the work, and whether the entry is billable.

Ownership (which employee the timelog belongs to) and timesheet assignment are managed through separate workflows and cannot be changed through this endpoint. Timelogs that are part of an approved timesheet are immutable regardless of the caller's permissions.
IErpHrmTimelog.IUpdate.x-autobe-specification: Maps erp_hrm_timelogs columns: date (required, calendar date stored as Timestamptz), duration_minutes (required, positive integer), project_id (required, UUID referencing erp_hrm_projects — project must be active and timelog owner must be a project member), billable (required, boolean, default true for new timelogs). Optional-nullable: task_id (UUID | null — when provided must reference a task whose project_id matches the supplied project_id; set to null to clear task association), description (free-text | null — set to null to clear). Excluded: id (PK identified via path parameter timelogId), employee_id (ownership immutable — resolved from JWT session), timesheet_id (managed via timesheet workflow endpoints), created_at/updated_at/deleted_at (system-managed timestamps), all BELONGS-TO relations (employee, project, task, timesheet) kept as scalar FK IDs per Request DTO convention.

projects.description:
Per-project budget comparison items showing estimated versus actual hours.

Each item represents one project that has a defined budget, regardless of its status (active, archived, or completed). Projects without budget hours are excluded. Projects with no timelogs logged still appear with zero actual hours and zero percent utilization.

The list includes a utilization percentage computed as actual hours divided by budget hours, helping managers quickly identify over-budget or under-utilized projects.
projects.x-autobe-specification:
Computed array sourced from LEFT JOIN of erp_hrm_projects (filtered: organization_id = current context, deleted_at IS NULL, budget_hours IS NOT NULL) with erp_hrm_timelogs (filtered: deleted_at IS NULL) ON timelogs.project_id = projects.id, grouped by project_id.

Each element is an IErpHrmProjectBudgetReport.IItem containing: project_id, project_name (from erp_hrm_projects.name), budget_hours (from erp_hrm_projects.budget_hours), actual_hours (SUM(timelogs.duration_minutes) / 60), utilization_percentage ((actual_hours / budget_hours) * 100), and project_status (from erp_hrm_projects.status). Projects with zero timelogs yield actual_hours = 0 and utilization_percentage = 0.

Both billable and non-billable timelogs are included. No individual timelog details or employee-level data are exposed.

summary.description:
Organization-wide summary totals for the project budget report.

Provides aggregate figures across all included projects: total budget hours (sum of all project estimates), total actual hours (sum of all logged hours), and overall utilization percentage (actual divided by budget across the entire organization).

This summary gives leadership a single-number health check on how the organization's project time budgets are being consumed overall.
summary.x-autobe-specification:
Computed totals aggregated across all qualifying projects in the response.

total_budget_hours = SUM(erp_hrm_projects.budget_hours) across all projects meeting filter criteria.
total_actual_hours = SUM(actual_hours) across all items in the projects array.
overall_utilization = (total_actual_hours / total_budget_hours) * 100.

If total_budget_hours is 0 (no qualifying projects), overall_utilization should be 0 to avoid division by zero.

IErpHrmProjectBudgetReport.description:
Project budget report comparing planned budget hours against actual logged hours across all projects within the current organization.

Each project with a defined budget appears in the list with its estimated hours, actual logged hours, and a computed utilization percentage. Projects without any timelogs are included with zero actual hours, ensuring the report reflects the full budget picture.

The summary section provides organization-wide totals for budget hours, actual hours, and overall utilization rate. Both billable and non-billable timelogs are included in actual hour calculations. Projects without budget hours set are excluded from the report entirely.
IErpHrmProjectBudgetReport.x-autobe-specification:
Aggregation report sourced from erp_hrm_projects (filtered: deleted_at IS NULL, budget_hours IS NOT NULL, organization_id matches authenticated user's current organization context) left-joined with erp_hrm_timelogs (filtered: deleted_at IS NULL) on timelogs.project_id = projects.id.

Per-project computation: actual_hours = SUM(erp_hrm_timelogs.duration_minutes) / 60 grouped by project_id, including both billable and non-billable timelogs. utilization_percentage = (actual_hours / budget_hours) * 100. Projects with zero timelogs yield actual_hours = 0 and utilization_percentage = 0.

Summary computation: total_budget_hours = SUM of all budget_hours across qualifying projects. total_actual_hours = SUM of all actual_hours. overall_utilization = (total_actual_hours / total_budget_hours) * 100.

Authorization: Requires report:view permission. All queries scoped to the authenticated user's current organization context. No individual timelog descriptions or employee-level details are exposed — this is aggregate-only.

email.description:
The registered email address of the member requesting a password reset.

Must be a valid email address in standard format (e.g., user@example.com). The system uses this email to locate the corresponding member account and deliver the reset token.

For security, malformed email formats are rejected with a 400 Bad Request before any database lookup. If the email is valid but does not match any active member account, the system still returns 204 No Content — the same response as a successful request — to prevent attackers from discovering which email addresses are registered.
email.x-autobe-specification: Cross-table lookup: the email is matched against erp_hrm_members.email (WHERE deleted_at IS NULL) to resolve the target member's UUID as erp_hrm_member_id. The email itself is never stored in erp_hrm_member_password_resets. Validate email format (RFC 5322) before performing the lookup. Return 204 regardless of match result to prevent email enumeration.

IErpHrmMemberPasswordReset.ICreate.description:
Request body for initiating a password reset flow.

The member provides their registered email address to request a password reset token. The system generates a time-limited, cryptographically secure token and sends it to the email address if a matching active member account exists.

For privacy and security, the response always returns 204 No Content regardless of whether the email address is registered. This prevents attackers from enumerating registered email addresses. Tokens are single-use and expire after a configurable duration.
IErpHrmMemberPasswordReset.ICreate.x-autobe-specification:
Accepts the member's registered email address for initiating a password reset. The email is used to look up the member in erp_hrm_members (WHERE deleted_at IS NULL) to resolve erp_hrm_member_id. All other fields are auto-generated by the system: id (UUID), token (cryptographically secure random string, globally unique via @@unique([token])), created_at and updated_at (current timestamp), expired_at (configurable duration from now), erp_hrm_member_id (resolved from the email lookup). Before creating a new token, any existing unused tokens for the resolved member are deleted to prevent token accumulation. The token is sent to the member's email address via email service.

Edge cases: rate-limit requests per IP and per email to prevent abuse. Reject malformed email formats with 400 Bad Request before any database lookup. Return 204 No Content regardless of whether the email exists — do not reveal email enumeration. This endpoint is accessible to both guests and authenticated members.

weeks.description:
Weekly summary entries, one per ISO week within the report date range.

Each entry covers a Monday-to-Sunday week and includes total hours, billable versus non-billable breakdown, timelog count, and per-project and per-employee breakdowns. Weeks are ordered chronologically by start date.

When no timelogs match the query criteria, this array is empty rather than absent.
weeks.x-autobe-specification:
Computed array of weekly summary entries, each representing one ISO week (Monday-Sunday) within the report date range.

Computation:
1. Query erp_hrm_timelogs joined with erp_hrm_employees and erp_hrm_projects, filtered by organization scope, date range [startDate, endDate], and optional projectId.
2. GROUP BY ISO week. For each week, compute aggregate statistics: totalHours, billableHours, nonBillableHours, totalTimelogs, projectBreakdown (per-project), employeeBreakdown (per-employee).
3. Each week entry maps to IErpHrmWeeklySummaryReport.IWeek with weekStartDate, weekEndDate, and all aggregated metrics.
4. Sort by weekStartDate ascending.
5. All hour values rounded to 2 decimal places.

If no timelogs match the criteria, return an empty array (not null, not 404).

IErpHrmWeeklySummaryReport.description:
Weekly summary report aggregating time tracking data for an organization.

Groups timelogs by ISO week (Monday through Sunday) within the specified date range, providing total hours, billable versus non-billable hour breakdowns, and per-project and per-employee summaries for each week. Only members with the `report:view` permission can access this report.

All data is scoped to the member's currently selected organization. Individual timelog descriptions and notes are never exposed — only aggregated statistics at the week, project, and employee level are returned. Deactivated employees' historical data is included in aggregates.
IErpHrmWeeklySummaryReport.x-autobe-specification:
Computed report aggregating timelog data across the organization, scoped to the member's currently selected organization context.

Source tables: erp_hrm_timelogs (duration_minutes, billable, date), erp_hrm_employees (id, name via erp_hrm_members), erp_hrm_projects (id, name).

Authorization: Requires `report:view` permission. Returns 403 Forbidden if the member lacks this permission.

Query Parameters:
- startDate (required): ISO 8601 date string defining the start of the report period. Filter timelogs where date >= startDate.
- endDate (required): ISO 8601 date string defining the end of the report period. Filter timelogs where date <= endDate.
- projectId (optional): UUID string. When provided, filter timelogs to only those belonging to the specified project within the organization. When omitted, include all projects.

Aggregation Logic:
1. Query erp_hrm_timelogs joined with erp_hrm_employees (on employee_id) and erp_hrm_projects (on project_id).
2. Filter: employee's erp_hrm_organization_id matches the member's selected organization, deleted_at IS NULL on all joined tables, timelog date within [startDate, endDate].
3. When projectId is provided, additionally filter project_id = projectId.
4. Group timelogs by ISO week (Monday-Sunday). For each week compute:
   - weekStartDate: Monday of that week
   - weekEndDate: Sunday of that week
   - totalHours: SUM(duration_minutes) / 60 across all matching timelogs
   - billableHours: SUM(duration_minutes) / 60 where billable = true
   - nonBillableHours: totalHours - billableHours
   - totalTimelogs: COUNT of timelog records
   - projectBreakdown: array of per-project summaries (projectId, projectName, totalHours, billableHours, timelogCount)
   - employeeBreakdown: array of per-employee summaries (employeeId, employeeName, totalHours, billableHours, timelogCount)
5. Round all hour values to 2 decimal places.
6. Sort weeks chronologically by weekStartDate ascending.

Privacy: No individual timelog descriptions or notes exposed. Employee breakdown shows only aggregated hours — individual timelog details are never included. Deactivated employees' historical data is included in aggregates.

Edge cases: Empty result set returns { weeks: [] } (not 404). If startDate is after endDate, return 400 Bad Request. Date range may span multiple weeks; each week is computed independently.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the timelog entry.

A UUID v4 string that uniquely identifies this timelog across all organizations. Automatically assigned by the server when the timelog is created and never modified thereafter.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timelogs.id. UUID v4 primary key, auto-generated on creation. Immutable after creation.

date.description:
The calendar date on which the work was performed.

Represents the day when the work took place, stored as a date-time value for database consistency but treated as date-only. Used for chronological ordering, timesheet week calculations, and time reporting across date ranges.
date.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timelogs.date. Stored as Timestamptz in the database but semantically represents a date-only value (no time component meaningful). Must be a valid calendar date.

duration_minutes.description:
The length of the work session in minutes.

Represents the total time worked during this entry. Used in aggregate calculations for timesheet total hours, project budget tracking, and employee time reports. Normal entries have positive values. A value of zero is possible only in the rare edge case where a live timer was started and immediately stopped.
duration_minutes.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timelogs.duration_minutes. Integer value representing the length of the work session in minutes. Must be non-negative (≥0). Positive for normal entries. Zero (0) only occurs in the edge case where a timer is started and immediately stopped within ~29 seconds (duration rounds to 0).

description.description:
Optional free-text description of the work performed during this time entry.

Provides context about what was accomplished, enabling employees and managers to understand the nature of the work at a glance. Supports full-text search for finding timelogs by descriptive content. May be null when the employee chose not to provide a description.
description.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timelogs.description. Nullable free-text field. Supports full-text search via GIN trigram index on the database. May be null when no description was provided.

billable.description:
Indicates whether this time entry is billable to the client.

Billable timelogs are included in billable hour calculations for time reports and project budget reports. Non-billable timelogs represent internal work, administrative tasks, or other activities that are not charged to the client. Defaults to true for newly created timelogs.
billable.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timelogs.billable. Boolean value. Defaults to true when not explicitly specified during creation. Used by time reports and project budget reports to distinguish billable from non-billable hours.

employee.description:
The employee who performed the work recorded in this timelog.

Includes the employee's summary profile: their member identity (display name, email, avatar), assigned role within the organization, optional department, position title, employment type classification, and current active or deactivated status.
employee.x-autobe-specification: JOIN via erp_hrm_timelogs.employee_id → erp_hrm_employees.id. Returns IErpHrmEmployee.ISummary with the employee's member profile, role, department, position, employment type, and status. The employee must belong to the same organization as the requesting user.

project.description:
The project against which the time was logged.

Identifies the project this work belongs to. The summary includes the project name, its visual color code for UI display, the current lifecycle status (active, archived, or completed), and an optional description. All timelogs must be logged against an active project.
project.x-autobe-specification: JOIN via erp_hrm_timelogs.project_id → erp_hrm_projects.id. Returns IErpHrmProject.ISummary with the project's name, color code, status, and optional description. The project must belong to the same organization as the timelog.

task.description:
The optional task within the project that this timelog is logged against.

Provides granular tracking at the task level when the work was performed on a specific task within the project. When null, the timelog is logged against the project as a whole without a specific task association. The task summary includes the title, status, priority, due date, estimated hours, and assigned employee.
task.x-autobe-specification: JOIN via erp_hrm_timelogs.task_id → erp_hrm_tasks.id. Returns IErpHrmTask.ISummary when a task is assigned, or null when no specific task was targeted. The task must belong to the same project referenced by the timelog's project_id.

timesheet.description:
The optional timesheet that groups this timelog for weekly submission and approval.

When a timelog is added to a timesheet, it becomes part of that timesheet's workflow. Once the timesheet is approved, the timelog becomes immutable. When null, the timelog is ungrouped and freely editable by its owner or by users with the time:manage permission. The timesheet summary includes the calendar week range, current status, total hours, and submission timestamp.
timesheet.x-autobe-specification: JOIN via erp_hrm_timelogs.timesheet_id → erp_hrm_timesheets.id. Returns IErpHrmTimesheet.ISummary when the timelog is grouped into a timesheet, or null when the timelog is ungrouped. When set, the timelog is subject to the timesheet's workflow constraints.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the timelog was initially created.

Automatically set by the server at the moment of creation and never modified thereafter. Used for audit trails, chronological ordering, and synchronization purposes.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timelogs.created_at. Timestamptz set automatically on INSERT. Immutable after creation — never modified by updates.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent modification to the timelog.

Automatically updated by the server whenever any field of the timelog changes, including date, duration, project, task, description, billable status, or timesheet assignment. Used for tracking when the record was last altered.
updated_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timelogs.updated_at. Timestamptz automatically updated on every modification to the timelog record. Tracks the most recent change regardless of which field was modified.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the timelog.

When null, the timelog is active and visible in normal queries. When set, the timelog is considered deleted but its record is preserved for audit integrity. Deletion is only permitted when the timelog is not part of a submitted or approved timesheet.
deleted_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timelogs.deleted_at. Nullable Timestamptz. Null for active timelogs. Set to the deletion timestamp when the timelog is soft-deleted. Deletion is blocked when the timelog belongs to a submitted or approved timesheet.

IErpHrmTimelog.description:
A complete timelog record representing work performed by an employee on a specific date.

Each timelog captures a duration in minutes logged against a required project, with an optional task within that project for granular tracking. The billable flag distinguishes billable from non-billable work for reporting purposes.

Timelogs may optionally be grouped into a timesheet for weekly submission and approval. Once a timesheet containing a timelog is approved, the timelog becomes immutable — no fields can be changed. Timelogs belonging to submitted or approved timesheets cannot be deleted, and those in approved timesheets cannot be edited. Ungrouped timelogs (those without a timesheet association) remain freely editable by their owner or by users with the time:manage permission.

The employee field identifies who performed the work, the project field indicates which project the work belongs to, and the optional task field provides granular tracking within that project. The optional timesheet field shows the parent timesheet when the timelog has been grouped for weekly submission.
IErpHrmTimelog.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_timelogs table. Scalar columns: id (UUID PK, auto-generated), date (calendar date stored as Timestamptz, semantically date-only), duration_minutes (integer ≥0, positive for normal entries, 0 only from immediate timer-stop edge case), description (nullable free-text with GIN trigram index for full-text search), billable (boolean, default true), created_at (auto-set on INSERT, immutable), updated_at (auto-updated on every modification), deleted_at (nullable soft-delete timestamp, set on deletion). Relations via JOIN: employee (erp_hrm_employees via employee_id → IErpHrmEmployee.ISummary), project (erp_hrm_projects via project_id → IErpHrmProject.ISummary), task (erp_hrm_tasks via task_id → IErpHrmTask.ISummary, nullable), timesheet (erp_hrm_timesheets via timesheet_id → IErpHrmTimesheet.ISummary, nullable). All BELONGS-TO FK ID columns replaced with .ISummary $ref objects per Read DTO convention. Timelogs are leaf entities with no HAS-MANY relations. Organization scoping enforced through JOIN via employee → erp_hrm_organization_id matching session context. Soft-deleted records (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) excluded from normal queries; returned only when explicitly requested.

action_type.description:
Filters activity log entries by the type of action performed.

Matches entries where the action_type column equals the specified value exactly. Recognized action types include employee_invited, employee_deactivated, employee_reactivated, contract_created, contract_edited, project_created, project_archived, project_completed, project_deleted, task_status_changed, timesheet_submitted, timesheet_approved, timesheet_rejected, role_assigned, and role_changed.

When not provided, no action type filter is applied and entries of all types are included in the results.
action_type.x-autobe-specification: Exact match filter against the action_type column of erp_hrm_activity_logs. Applied as WHERE action_type = :value when provided. Optional — omitted filter means all action types are included.

user_id.description:
Filters activity log entries by the user who performed the action.

Matches entries where the user_id column equals the specified UUID exactly. Use this to trace all actions performed by a specific member within the organization.

When not provided, no user filter is applied and entries from all users are included in the results.
user_id.x-autobe-specification: Exact match filter against the user_id column of erp_hrm_activity_logs. Applied as WHERE user_id = :value when provided. Optional — omitted filter means entries from all users are included.

date_from.description:
Filters activity log entries to those created on or after this date and time.

Applied as an inclusive lower bound on the created_at column. Combined with date_to to form a date range filter. Both date_from and date_to must be valid ISO-8601 datetime strings.

When not provided, no lower date bound is applied and all entries from the beginning of time are included.
date_from.x-autobe-specification: Inclusive lower bound filter on the created_at column of erp_hrm_activity_logs. Applied as WHERE created_at >= :date_from when provided. Used together with date_to to form a date range. Optional — omitted means no lower bound.

date_to.description:
Filters activity log entries to those created on or before this date and time.

Applied as an inclusive upper bound on the created_at column. Combined with date_from to form a date range filter. Both date_from and date_to must be valid ISO-8601 datetime strings.

When not provided, no upper date bound is applied and entries up to the present moment are included.
date_to.x-autobe-specification: Inclusive upper bound filter on the created_at column of erp_hrm_activity_logs. Applied as WHERE created_at <= :date_to when provided. Used together with date_from to form a date range. Optional — omitted means no upper bound.

page.description:
The page number to retrieve, starting from 1.

Used for offset-based pagination through activity log results. The first page is page 1, not page 0. This value is validated and bounds-checked against the total number of pages available for the current filter criteria.

When not provided, defaults to 1, returning the first page of results.
page.x-autobe-specification: 1-based page number for offset-based pagination. Applied as OFFSET = (page - 1) * limit in the SQL query. Defaults to 1 when not provided. Validated and bounds-checked against the total page count: if page exceeds total pages, an empty result set is returned.

limit.description:
The maximum number of records to return per page.

Controls page size for paginated activity log results. Must be between 1 and 100 inclusive. The actual number of records returned may be less than this value on the final page or when total records are fewer than the limit.

When not provided, a default limit is applied by the server.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Maximum records per page for offset-based pagination. Applied as LIMIT in the SQL query. Must be between 1 and 100 inclusive. A server-side default is applied when not provided.

IErpHrmActivityLog.IRequest.description:
Search criteria for filtering activity log entries with pagination.

Activity logs provide an immutable, append-only audit trail of significant actions across the organization. Each entry records who performed what action, on which entity, at what time. This request DTO supports filtering by action type (e.g., employee_invited, task_status_changed, timesheet_approved), by the user who performed the action, or by a date range.

Multiple filters can be combined to narrow results. When no filters are provided, all activity logs for the organization are returned. Results are paginated and sorted in reverse chronological order (most recent first).
IErpHrmActivityLog.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: Filters map directly to erp_hrm_activity_logs columns: action_type (exact match), user_id (exact match), date_from/date_to (inclusive range on created_at). Pagination: page (1-based, defaults to 1), limit (1-100, default applied by server). Results sorted by created_at DESC by default. All fields optional — empty body returns all logs for the organization in reverse chronological order. organization_id is resolved from session context and never exposed in the request body.

id.description:
Primary key uniquely identifying the activity log entry.

The `id` is a UUID v4 generated server-side when the activity log entry is created. It serves as the unique identifier for retrieval via the single-entry endpoint (`GET /erpHrm/member/activity-logs/{activityLogId}`).
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_activity_logs.id. Primary key, UUID v4, auto-generated server-side on log entry creation. Used as the path parameter (`activityLogId`) in the single-entry retrieval endpoint.

action_type.description:
Category label classifying the nature of the action performed.

Recognized action types include: `employee_invited` (a new employee invitation was sent), `employee_deactivated` (an active employee was suspended), `employee_reactivated` (a deactivated employee was restored), `contract_created` (a new employment contract was created), `contract_edited` (an existing contract was modified), `project_created` (a new project was created), `project_archived` (a project was archived), `project_completed` (a project was marked complete), `project_deleted` (a project was permanently removed), `task_status_changed` (a task moved to a different status), `timesheet_submitted` (a timesheet was submitted for review), `timesheet_approved` (a submitted timesheet was approved), `timesheet_rejected` (a submitted timesheet was rejected and returned to draft), `role_assigned` (a role was assigned to an employee), and `role_changed` (an employee's role was changed to a different one).
action_type.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_activity_logs.action_type. Category label classifying the nature of the action performed. No transformation or enum validation — returned as stored in the database.

target_entity.description:
The type of business object affected by the action.

Together with `target_id`, this forms a polymorphic reference that identifies the specific entity instance that was created, modified, or transitioned. Values correspond to entity type names such as `employee`, `contract`, `project`, `task`, `timesheet`, or `role`. The actual database table is determined by this value — it is not a foreign key since it can reference multiple different entity types.
target_entity.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_activity_logs.target_entity. The type name of the business object affected by the action. Together with target_id, forms a polymorphic reference — no foreign key constraint exists since it can point to multiple entity types. Returned as stored without transformation.

target_id.description:
The unique identifier of the specific business object affected by the action.

This is a polymorphic reference — the actual table and entity type are determined by the accompanying `target_entity` field. It is a UUID that identifies the specific instance (e.g., a particular project, task, or timesheet) that was the subject of the recorded action.
target_id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_activity_logs.target_id. UUID of the affected entity instance. Polymorphic reference — the target table is determined by target_entity. Stored as UUID but not a foreign key; no referential integrity constraint enforced at the database level.

details.description:
Optional contextual information stored as a JSON string, supplementing the action record with action-type-specific data.

The content of this field varies by the `action_type`:
- **Task status changes** (`task_status_changed`): Contains old and new status values — `{"old_status": "in_progress", "new_status": "completed"}`
- **Timesheet rejections** (`timesheet_rejected`): Contains the rejection reason — `{"reason": "Hours do not match project allocation"}`
- **Contract edits** (`contract_edited`): Contains the list of changed fields — `{"changed_fields": ["pay_rate", "pay_period"]}`

This field is `null` when no additional contextual information is available for the recorded action.
details.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_activity_logs.details. Nullable JSON string — returned as-is without parsing or transformation. Null when no additional contextual information exists for the recorded action. Content structure varies by action_type: task status changes contain `{"old_status": "...", "new_status": "..."}`, timesheet rejections contain `{"reason": "..."}`, contract edits contain `{"changed_fields": [...]}`.

created_at.description:
The exact date and time when the action was completed and this log entry was recorded.

Formatted as an ISO 8601 timestamp with timezone. This is the sole temporal field on activity log entries — since entries are append-only and immutable, there is no `updated_at` counterpart. The timestamp reflects when the server recorded the action, not when the action was initiated.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_activity_logs.created_at. ISO 8601 timestamp with timezone (Timestamptz). This is the sole temporal field — activity log entries are append-only and immutable, so there is no updated_at counterpart. Reflects when the server recorded the action.

organization_id.description:
The organization where the action occurred.

Enforces multi-tenancy data isolation — activity logs are always scoped to a single organization. Users can only view logs for their currently selected organization context. This value is set server-side based on the authenticated user's active organization at the time the action was performed.
organization_id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_activity_logs.organization_id. UUID of the organization where the action occurred. Always scoped to the authenticated user's currently selected organization context — cross-organization access is forbidden. IErpHrmActivityLog.description:
An immutable audit trail entry recording a significant business action within an organization.

Each activity log entry captures who performed what action on which entity at what time, forming the organization's permanent chronological record of operational changes. The log is append-only — entries are never modified or deleted once created.

**Actor**: The `user` property identifies the member who performed the action, establishing individual accountability for every recorded event. Every entry has a known actor — this field is never null.

**Action Classification**: The `action_type` field categorizes the nature of the action. Recognized types include `employee_invited`, `employee_deactivated`, `employee_reactivated`, `contract_created`, `contract_edited`, `project_created`, `project_archived`, `project_completed`, `project_deleted`, `task_status_changed`, `timesheet_submitted`, `timesheet_approved`, `timesheet_rejected`, `role_assigned`, and `role_changed`.

**Target Identification**: The `target_entity` and `target_id` fields together form a polymorphic reference identifying the specific business object affected by the action. `target_entity` specifies the entity type (e.g., `employee`, `contract`, `project`, `task`, `timesheet`, `role`), while `target_id` holds the UUID of the affected instance. This is not a foreign key — it can reference multiple different entity types.

**Contextual Details**: The `details` field stores action-type-specific contextual information as a JSON string. Examples include old and new status values for task status changes (`{"old_status": "in_progress", "new_status": "completed"}`), rejection reasons for timesheet rejections (`{"reason": "Hours exceed project allocation"}`), or changed fields for contract edits (`{"changed_fields": ["pay_rate", "pay_period"]}`). This field is `null` when no additional context is available.

**Access Control**: Activity log entries are scoped to the currently selected organization context via `organization_id`. Access is restricted to users holding the organization management permission — cross-organization access is not permitted, and a 403 Forbidden is returned for unauthorized actors.

**Immutability**: Entries are append-only and immutable. They are never modified or deleted through any user-facing operation. Removal only occurs via cascading deletion when the owning organization is permanently deleted.
IErpHrmActivityLog.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_activity_logs for scalar columns: id (UUID PK), action_type (category label, returned as stored), target_entity (entity type name), target_id (UUID of affected entity, polymorphic — no FK constraint), details (nullable JSON string, returned as-is without parsing), created_at (ISO 8601 timestamptz, sole temporal field — entries are immutable), organization_id (UUID scoping to current org). The user relation is resolved via BELONGS-TO JOIN on user_id → erp_hrm_members.id, returning IErpHrmMember.ISummary (consolidated view of global profile + org-specific employment details). The raw user_id FK column is intentionally excluded — surfaced through the user object. No insert/update/delete DTOs exist — activity logs are append-only, created server-side during business operations, and never modified through any user-facing endpoint.

IErpHrmMemberSession.ISwitchOrganization.description:
Request body for switching the active organization context of the current session.

After a successful switch, the member's effective permissions reflect the role they hold in the newly selected organization. Data from the previous organization becomes inaccessible until the member switches back.

If the target organization is the same as the currently active one, the operation is treated as a no-op and returns success.

token.description:
The verification token string delivered to the user's email address.

A cryptographically secure, globally unique token generated during the sign-up process and included in the verification email sent to the user. Submitting this token confirms that the user owns the email address associated with the verification record.

The token is single-use — once successfully verified, the corresponding record's `verified_at` field is populated and the token becomes consumed. Subsequent submissions of the same token return a success response (idempotent behavior) rather than an error.

All other fields are derived from the matched database record.

IErpHrmMemberEmailVerification.ICreate.description:

Upon successful verification, the system automatically matches any pending organization invitations targeting the verified email address and enrolls the user into those organizations. Verification is idempotent — submitting an already-verified token returns a success response rather than an error.

cursor.description:
Cursor for keyset-based pagination, representing the `created_at` timestamp of the last entry from the previous page.

When provided alongside `limit`, the response returns history entries whose `created_at` timestamp is strictly greater than the cursor value, ordered chronologically ascending. page.description:

When provided alongside `limit`, the API skips `(page - 1) × limit` records and returns the next `limit` records. Page numbering starts from 1, with the first page being page 1. IErpHrmTaskHistory.IRequest.description:
Request filters and pagination parameters for querying task status change history.

Task history entries are immutable audit trail records created automatically when a task's status transitions. This request DTO provides optional filters to narrow results by the old and new status values, the member who performed the change, and the date range when the change occurred. Multiple status values can be selected simultaneously for both old and new status filters.

Pagination supports both cursor-based pagination using a `cursor` value derived from the `created_at` timestamp combined with `limit`, and offset-based pagination using `page` and `limit`. Results are always returned in chronological order by `created_at` ascending (oldest history entries first).

Maps old_statuses → erp_hrm_task_histories.old_status (IN filter with multiple allowed values: open, in-progress, completed, closed), new_statuses → erp_hrm_task_histories.new_status (IN filter with multiple allowed values: open, in-progress, completed, closed), changed_by_member_id → erp_hrm_task_histories.changed_by_member_id (equality match against UUID), created_from/created_to → erp_hrm_task_histories.created_at (inclusive range: created_at >= created_from AND created_at <= created_to). Pagination: cursor-based uses cursor (created_at value for keyset pagination) + limit; offset-based uses page (1-indexed) + limit. Excludes history entries where the parent task's deleted_at is set. Results always ordered by created_at ascending (oldest first). All filters are optional; when none are specified, returns all history entries for the task.

Contains essential time tracking fields: the work date, duration in minutes, and billable classification. Provides contextual relationships to the employee who performed the work, the project time was logged against, and optionally the specific task and enclosing timesheet.

Large free-text descriptions are excluded for list efficiency. All related entities are represented in their summary form for compact display.

IErpHrmTimesheet.IRequest.description:
Search, filter, and pagination parameters for listing timesheets.

All properties are optional — omit them to retrieve an unfiltered paginated list of timesheets scoped to the current organization context and the calling user's permissions. The response adapts automatically to the caller's role, limiting visibility to owned timesheets for regular employees and providing organization-wide access for managers and approvers.

**Status Filtering**: Pass one or more status values (draft, submitted, approved, rejected) to narrow results by workflow state. When multiple values are provided, timesheets matching any of the specified statuses are returned.

**Date Range Filtering**: Provide a dateRange with start and end dates to find timesheets whose calendar week overlaps with the specified period. Useful for locating timesheets within a particular month, quarter, or custom date range.

**Employee Filtering**: The employeeId filter is available only to users with time:view_all or time approval permission. Employees without elevated permissions receive a permission-denied error if they specify another employee's ID.

**Pagination**: Use page and limit for offset-based pagination. Results are ordered by created_at descending by default, but can be customized via sort.
IErpHrmTimesheet.IRequest.x-autobe-specification:
Search, filter, and pagination parameters for the timesheet listing endpoint (PATCH /erpHrm/member/timesheets).

This is a request body DTO — it does not map to any single database table. Each property translates to a WHERE, ORDER BY, or pagination clause in the query against erp_hrm_timesheets.

**Authorization Scoping**: The query automatically scopes to the current organization context. Additionally:
- Users with `time:view_all` or time approval permission see all non-deleted timesheets in the organization.
- Regular employees see only their own timesheets (WHERE employee_id = requesting employee's record).
- Exclude soft-deleted timesheets (deleted_at IS NOT NULL).

**Filter Mapping**:
- status: WHERE status IN (values) — filter by one or more workflow states.
- dateRange: WHERE week_start_date <= dateRange.end AND week_end_date >= dateRange.start — overlap filter returning any timesheet whose calendar week intersects the requested range.
- employeeId: WHERE employee_id = value — only honored when caller has time:view_all or time approval permission; otherwise rejected for cross-employee queries.

**Pagination**:
- page: OFFSET-based pagination, 1-indexed. Calculated as (page - 1) * limit.
- limit: Clamped to 1–100 range. Defaults to server-defined value when omitted.
- sort: ORDER BY clause. Must be SQL-safe — only allow known column names (id, week_start_date, status, submitted_at, created_at) with ASC/DESC direction. Defaults to created_at DESC.

The collection of aggregated report entries, each discriminated by its grouping dimension.

When grouped by employee, each entry includes the employee's name alongside hour totals. When grouped by project, the project name appears with aggregated metrics. When grouped by task, task titles are included — timelogs without a task assignment are consolidated under an "Unassigned" entry.

An empty array indicates no timelogs matched the query filters for the specified date range. This is a valid response and does not indicate an error.
data.x-autobe-specification:
Aggregated results array computed from erp_hrm_timelogs query, discriminated by group_by field.

**Discriminator**: `group_by` — determines which variant schema each array element conforms to:
- `employee` → IErpHrmTimeReport.IEmployeeGroup (grouped by employee_id with display_name)
- `project` → IErpHrmTimeReport.IProjectGroup (grouped by project_id with project name)
- `task` → IErpHrmTimeReport.ITaskGroup (grouped by task_id with task title; null task_id entries appear as 'Unassigned')
- `grand_total` → IErpHrmTimeReport.IGrandTotal (single organization-wide summary when no groupBy specified)

Each variant contains the same core metrics (total_hours, billable_hours, non_billable_hours, entry_count) plus variant-specific identifier fields. The array may be empty when no timelogs match the query criteria — a 404 must NOT be returned.

IErpHrmTimeReport.description:
An aggregated time report summarizing logged work hours across the organization for a specified date range.

Results are grouped by the chosen dimension — employee, project, or task — with separate tallies for billable and non-billable hours alongside entry counts. When no grouping is specified, a single organization-wide grand total is returned.

All hour values are computed from aggregated duration data rounded to two decimal places. Individual timelog details such as personal notes and descriptions are not included in this report, ensuring privacy compliance while providing actionable workforce and project insights.
IErpHrmTimeReport.x-autobe-specification:
Computed report from erp_hrm_timelogs aggregated by the groupBy query parameter, scoped to the member's active organization context via session.

**Data Source**: erp_hrm_timelogs table, with JOINs:
- erp_hrm_employees (via employee_id) for employee display_name
- erp_hrm_projects (via project_id) for project name
- erp_hrm_tasks (via task_id) for task title

**Aggregation Formulas**:
- total_hours = SUM(duration_minutes) / 60
- billable_hours = SUM(duration_minutes WHERE billable = true) / 60
- non_billable_hours = SUM(duration_minutes WHERE billable = false) / 60
- entry_count = COUNT(*)

**Grouping Behavior**:
- groupBy = 'employee': groups by employee_id, includes employee name via JOIN
- groupBy = 'project': groups by project_id, includes project name via JOIN
- groupBy = 'task': groups by task_id, includes task title via JOIN; timelogs with null task_id consolidated under synthetic entry with taskId: null and title: 'Unassigned'
- groupBy omitted: single grand_total entry for the entire organization

**Edge Cases**:
- No matching timelogs: return data: [] (empty array, not 404)
- Task grouping: null task_id entries appear as 'Unassigned' category
- dateFrom after dateTo: reject with 400 before query execution

**Authorization**: Requires report:view permission. employeeId filter additionally requires time:view_all or time:manage permission. Reject with 403 if unauthorized.

**Privacy**: Individual timelog descriptions and personal notes are never included in the response; only aggregated numerical data and group identifiers are exposed.

active_employee_count.description:
The total number of currently active employees in the organization.

Counts all employee records within the currently selected organization whose status is active and who have not been soft-deleted. This metric provides an at-a-glance workforce size indicator for managers and owners.
active_employee_count.x-autobe-specification: COUNT of erp_hrm_employees where status = 'active' AND deleted_at IS NULL AND erp_hrm_organization_id matches the session-selected organization context. If no active employees exist, return 0 — never null.

total_hours_this_week.description:
The total work hours logged across the entire organization for the current calendar week (Monday–Sunday).

Aggregates all timelog durations — both billable and non-billable — converted from minutes to hours with two-decimal precision. The current week is determined using the organization's configured timezone. A value of zero indicates no time has been logged this week yet.
total_hours_this_week.x-autobe-specification: SUM(erp_hrm_timelogs.duration_minutes) / 60 for timelogs where date falls within the current Monday–Sunday week (computed server-side using the organization's configured timezone), deleted_at IS NULL on timelogs, and the owning employee's erp_hrm_organization_id matches session context (enforced via JOIN to erp_hrm_employees). Round to 2 decimal places. If no timelogs exist for the week, return 0 — never null.

pending_timesheets_count.description:
The number of timesheets currently submitted and awaiting approval within the organization.

Counts all submitted timesheets that have not yet been approved or rejected. This metric helps managers prioritize their review workload.
pending_timesheets_count.x-autobe-specification: COUNT of erp_hrm_timesheets where status = 'submitted' AND deleted_at IS NULL, joined through erp_hrm_employees to verify organization scope (erp_hrm_organization_id matches session context). If no pending timesheets exist, return 0 — never null.

projects_over_budget.description:
Projects whose actual logged hours exceed 80% of their budgeted hours.

Compares each project's planned budget against actual time logged through timelogs. Only projects with a defined budget are evaluated. Projects are ordered by utilization percentage, highest first. An empty array indicates no projects are approaching or exceeding their budget.
projects_over_budget.x-autobe-specification: For each project with a non-null budget_hours in erp_hrm_projects, calculate total minutes logged via erp_hrm_timelogs (excluding soft-deleted entries, scoped to session organization via JOIN through erp_hrm_employees). Compute utilization as (total_logged_minutes / 60) / budget_hours. Return projects where utilization > 0.80. Each item includes project_id (UUID), project_name (string), budget_hours (number), and actual_hours (number). Order by utilization descending. If no projects exceed 80% budget, return empty array — never null.

top_employees.description:
The top five employees ranked by total hours logged during the current calendar week.

Ranks active employees by their aggregated work hours for the current Monday-through-Sunday week, descending from most to least hours. Each entry identifies the employee by UUID and display name, along with their total hours with two-decimal precision. An empty array indicates no time has been logged this week.
top_employees.x-autobe-specification: Aggregate SUM(erp_hrm_timelogs.duration_minutes) per employee for the current Monday–Sunday week, JOIN erp_hrm_employees (filter: erp_hrm_organization_id matches session context, deleted_at IS NULL), JOIN erp_hrm_members for display_name. Exclude soft-deleted timelogs. GROUP BY employee_id, ORDER BY total_hours DESC, LIMIT 5. Each item includes employee_id (UUID), display_name (string), and total_hours (number, minutes/60 rounded to 2 decimals, ≥ 0). If no timelogs exist for the week, return empty array — never null.

IErpHrmOrganizationDashboard.description:
A top employee ranked by total hours logged during the current calendar week.

Represents one of the five employees with the highest aggregated work hours for the week within the currently selected organization. The total hours reflect the sum of all billable and non-billable timelog durations, converted from minutes to hours with two-decimal precision. This entry is part of the organization dashboard's top-employees metric, surfaced to managers and owners who hold the report:view permission.
IErpHrmOrganizationDashboard.x-autobe-specification:
Aggregated computation spanning three tables within the current organization context. Each row represents one of the top 5 employees ranked by total hours logged during the current calendar week (Monday–Sunday).

1. **employee_id**: Direct read from erp_hrm_employees.id. Filtered: erp_hrm_employees.erp_hrm_organization_id matches session-selected organization, deleted_at IS NULL.

2. **display_name**: JOIN erp_hrm_members ON erp_hrm_employees.member_id = erp_hrm_members.id, selecting erp_hrm_members.display_name. Both tables filtered for deleted_at IS NULL, organization scope via employee.

3. **total_hours**: SUM(erp_hrm_timelogs.duration_minutes) / 60 for timelogs where date falls within the current Monday–Sunday week (computed server-side using the organization's configured timezone), deleted_at IS NULL on timelogs, and the owning employee matches organization scope via JOIN to erp_hrm_employees. Round to 2 decimal places.

Overall: GROUP BY employee_id, ORDER BY total_hours DESC, LIMIT 5. If no timelogs exist for the week, return empty array — never null fields. Each row must satisfy: employee_id is non-null UUID, display_name is non-null string, total_hours is non-null number ≥ 0.

email.description:
The email address of the person to invite as an employee.

Must be a valid email format. Only one pending invitation per email address can exist within an organization at a time. If the invited email already belongs to an active employee in the organization, the request is rejected with a conflict error.
email.x-autobe-specification:
The email address of the person being invited. Validated for RFC 5322 email format. Used for duplicate detection: checked against existing pending invitations in the current organization (409 if duplicate), and against active employee emails (409 if already a member). Also used for invitation email delivery (fire-and-forget).

Organization context is implicit from the active session.

role_id.description:
The role to assign to the invited employee upon joining the organization.

References an existing role within the current organization. Built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) and custom roles are both accepted. The role determines the permissions the employee will have after accepting the invitation.
role_id.x-autobe-specification:
UUID referencing the role (erp_hrm_roles.id) the invitee will be assigned upon invitation fulfillment. Must exist and belong to the current organization context. Validated at invitation creation time to prevent dangling references.

When the invitation is resolved (recipient signs up with matching email), this role_id is used to create the employee record with the appropriate role assignment.

IErpHrmInvitation.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating an employee invitation.

Contains the email address of the person to invite and the role they will be assigned upon joining the organization. The invitation remains pending until the recipient signs up with the matching email address, at which point they are automatically added as an employee.

Only one pending invitation per email address can exist within an organization at a time. If the invited email already belongs to an active employee in the organization, the request is rejected with a conflict error.
IErpHrmInvitation.ICreate.x-autobe-specification:
This is a request-only DTO for invitation creation. It does not map to a single database table; the invitation record is built by combining the email and role_id from this DTO with the organization_id from the JWT session context, and a status of 'pending' is auto-assigned with the sent_at timestamp.

Validation: email must be valid format. Duplicate pending invitation for same email+org is rejected with 409. Existing active employee email is rejected with 409.

The role_id references erp_hrm_roles.id and determines the role the invitee receives upon fulfillment. Must be validated to exist within the current organization context.

hours_today_minutes.description:
Total minutes logged by the employee today.

Aggregates all timelog entries recorded on the current calendar date within the organization's timezone. Used to display daily time tracking progress. Returns zero when no time has been logged today.
hours_today_minutes.x-autobe-specification: SUM(erp_hrm_timelogs.duration_minutes) WHERE employee_id = current authenticated employee AND date = today's date in the organization's timezone. Respects deleted_at IS NULL on timelogs. Returns 0 when no timelogs exist for today.

hours_today_decimal_hours.description:
Total hours logged by the employee today, expressed as a decimal.

Calculated by dividing today's total minutes by 60. Provides a human-readable hours representation for dashboard display alongside the precise minute count. Returns zero when no time has been logged today.
hours_today_decimal_hours.x-autobe-specification: Derived from hours_today_minutes / 60.0. Uses the same underlying query: SUM(erp_hrm_timelogs.duration_minutes) WHERE employee_id = current AND date = today. Returns 0.0 when no timelogs exist for today.

hours_this_week_minutes.description:
Total minutes logged by the employee during the current calendar week.

Aggregates all timelog entries from Monday through Sunday of the current week based on the organization's timezone. Used to track weekly time tracking progress. Returns zero when no time has been logged this week.
hours_this_week_minutes.x-autobe-specification: SUM(erp_hrm_timelogs.duration_minutes) WHERE employee_id = current authenticated employee AND date BETWEEN Monday 00:00 and Sunday 23:59 of the current calendar week (determined from the organization's timezone). Respects deleted_at IS NULL on timelogs. Returns 0 when no timelogs exist for the current week.

hours_this_week_decimal_hours.description:
Total hours logged by the employee during the current calendar week, expressed as a decimal.

Calculated by dividing this week's total minutes by 60. Provides a human-readable hours representation for dashboard display alongside the precise minute count. Returns zero when no time has been logged this week.
hours_this_week_decimal_hours.x-autobe-specification: Derived from hours_this_week_minutes / 60.0. Uses the same underlying query: SUM(erp_hrm_timelogs.duration_minutes) WHERE employee_id = current AND date BETWEEN Monday 00:00 AND Sunday 23:59 of current calendar week. Returns 0.0 when no timelogs exist for the current week.

active_timer.description:
The employee's currently running timer, or null if no timer is active.

Represents a live time tracking session. An employee may have at most one active timer at any given time. When present, displays the project, optional task, description, and elapsed time since the timer was started. The elapsed time is computed as the difference between the current server time and the timer's start timestamp. Returns null when the employee has no running timer.
active_timer.x-autobe-specification: Query erp_hrm_timers WHERE erp_hrm_employee_id = current employee. At most one record due to @@unique constraint on erp_hrm_employee_id. When a timer exists, return the full IErpHrmTimer object with timer fields plus a computed elapsed_seconds = (NOW() - start_timestamp) as an integer. The downstream Realize agent MUST include this computed elapsed_seconds field in the timer response for dashboard context. When no active timer exists, return null.

recent_timelogs.description:
The five most recent timelog entries for the employee, ordered by creation time descending.

Provides a quick-access list of the employee's latest time tracking activity for dashboard display. Each entry includes the work date, duration, associated project and optional task, description, and billable status. When the timelog is part of a timesheet, the timesheet's status is included. Returns an empty array when no timelogs exist.
recent_timelogs.x-autobe-specification: SELECT the 5 most recent erp_hrm_timelogs WHERE employee_id = current employee AND deleted_at IS NULL, ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 5. Each entry resolves to IErpHrmTimelog.ISummary including: id, date, duration_minutes, project (id + name via JOIN to erp_hrm_projects), task (id + title via JOIN to erp_hrm_tasks if task_id is set), description, billable. If timesheet_id is set, JOIN erp_hrm_timesheets for status display. Returns an empty array when the employee has no timelogs.

pending_timesheet.description:
The timesheet for the current calendar week, or null if none has been created yet.

Represents the employee's weekly timesheet that groups timelogs for the Monday-to-Sunday period. Shows the timesheet's workflow status — draft, submitted, approved, or rejected — along with the week boundaries. When the timesheet has been rejected, includes the reviewer's rejection reason to guide the employee's revision. Returns null when no timesheet exists for the current week.
pending_timesheet.x-autobe-specification: Query erp_hrm_timesheets WHERE employee_id = current employee AND week_start_date = Monday of the current calendar week (organization timezone). When found, return IErpHrmTimesheet.ISummary including: id, status, week_start_date, week_end_date. When status is 'rejected', include rejection_reason for display. When no timesheet exists for the current week, return null.

assigned_tasks.description:
Tasks assigned to the employee that are currently open or in progress.

Lists the employee's active workload for triage on the dashboard. Tasks are ordered by priority level — urgent tasks appear first, followed by high, medium, and low priority — with secondary ordering by due date so that the most time-sensitive items are immediately visible. Each entry includes the task title, status, priority, due date, estimated hours, and the parent project's name. Returns an empty array when the employee has no open or in-progress assigned tasks.
assigned_tasks.x-autobe-specification: Query erp_hrm_tasks WHERE erp_hrm_assigned_employee_id = current employee AND status IN ('open', 'in-progress') AND deleted_at IS NULL. JOIN erp_hrm_projects for project id and name. ORDER BY priority (urgent first, then high, medium, low), due_date ASC with NULLS LAST. Each entry resolves to IErpHrmTask.ISummary including: id, title, status, priority, due_date, project (id + name), estimated_hours. Archived and completed projects with active tasks assigned to the employee should still appear. Returns an empty array when no open or in-progress tasks are assigned.

IErpHrmPersonalDashboard.description:
Aggregated personal dashboard for the authenticated employee, providing an at-a-glance summary of their current work status.

The dashboard combines time tracking progress (hours logged today and this week), active timer status, the five most recent time entries, the current week's timesheet, and open or in-progress assigned tasks into a single unified response. Designed for rendering a personal home screen where the employee can immediately see their daily and weekly progress, manage their active timer, review recent work, monitor timesheet submission status, and triage open tasks.

All data is strictly scoped to the authenticated employee within the currently selected organization. Each section is independently computed — if any section has no data, its fields gracefully default to zero, an empty array, or null rather than causing the entire request to fail. The employee must be active to access this endpoint; a deactivated employee receives a 403 response.
IErpHrmPersonalDashboard.x-autobe-specification:
Computed aggregation from multiple source tables scoped to the authenticated employee's organization context. No direct table mapping.

Source queries (all scoped to current employee, respecting deleted_at IS NULL on timelogs, timesheets, tasks, projects):

1. hours_today_minutes / hours_today_decimal_hours: SUM(erp_hrm_timelogs.duration_minutes) WHERE employee_id = current AND date = today (organization timezone). decimal_hours = minutes / 60.0.

2. hours_this_week_minutes / hours_this_week_decimal_hours: SUM(erp_hrm_timelogs.duration_minutes) WHERE employee_id = current AND date BETWEEN Monday 00:00 AND Sunday 23:59 of current calendar week (organization timezone). decimal_hours = minutes / 60.0.

3. active_timer: erp_hrm_timers WHERE erp_hrm_employee_id = current (at most one due to @@unique constraint). IMPORTANT: The downstream Realize agent MUST include computed elapsed_seconds = (NOW() - start_timestamp) as an integer in the timer response for this dashboard context. If no timer exists, return null. Additional fields required: id, start_timestamp, project (id + name via JOIN to erp_hrm_projects), task (id + title via JOIN to erp_hrm_tasks if task_id set), description.

4. recent_timelogs: 5 most recent erp_hrm_timelogs WHERE employee_id = current AND deleted_at IS NULL, ORDER BY created_at DESC. Include: id, date, duration_minutes, project (id + name), task (id + title), description, billable. If timesheet_id is set, JOIN erp_hrm_timesheets for status.

5. pending_timesheet: erp_hrm_timesheets WHERE employee_id = current AND week_start_date = Monday of current week. Include: id, status, week_start_date, week_end_date. If status is rejected, include rejection_reason. If no timesheet exists for current week, return null.

6. assigned_tasks: erp_hrm_tasks WHERE erp_hrm_assigned_employee_id = current AND status IN ('open', 'in-progress') AND deleted_at IS NULL. JOIN erp_hrm_projects for project name. ORDER BY priority (urgent > high > medium > low), due_date ASC NULLS LAST. Include: id, title, status, priority, due_date, project (id + name), estimated_hours.

Graceful defaults when no data: hours fields → 0, arrays → [], nullable objects → null. Employee must be active (status = 'active') — return 403 if deactivated.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the invitation.

A system-generated UUID assigned when the invitation record is created. Used to reference the invitation in subsequent operations such as revocation or status checks.
id.x-autobe-specification: System-generated UUID v4 assigned at invitation creation time. Not derived from any database column.

email.description:
The email address of the invited person.

The invitation is delivered to this email address. The recipient must sign up using the same email for the invitation to be automatically resolved. Only one pending invitation per email address can exist within an organization at any time.
email.x-autobe-specification: The email address the invitation was sent to. Must be unique among pending invitations within the same organization. Validated as a properly formatted email address. Used for matching when the recipient signs up.

status.description:
Current status of the invitation.

**pending**: The invitation has been sent but the recipient has not yet signed up with the matching email address. The invitation remains in this state indefinitely until fulfilled, revoked, or the organization is deleted.

**resolved**: The recipient has signed up with the matching email and has been automatically added as an employee of the organization with the assigned role.
status.x-autobe-specification: Enum discriminator with two possible values: 'pending' or 'resolved'. Set to 'pending' at invitation creation time. Transitions to 'resolved' when the recipient successfully signs up with the matching email address. No other valid transitions exist.

role.description:
The role assigned to the invitee upon joining the organization.

Determines the complete set of permissions the new employee will have once the invitation is resolved. The role is selected at invitation creation time and cannot be changed after the invitation is sent. Use the employee role change operation if a different role is needed after the employee joins.
role.x-autobe-specification: Resolved from the stored role_id by joining to erp_hrm_roles. Returns the ISummary of the role the invitee will receive upon joining. Includes id, name, is_builtin, description, permissions_count, created_at, and updated_at.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the invitation was sent.

Represents the exact moment the invitation record was created and the invitation email was dispatched to the recipient. This timestamp is immutable and provides an audit trail of when the invitation process began.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Timestamp recorded at the moment the invitation is created and the email is dispatched. Captured as server time at record creation. Immutable after creation.

resolved_at.description:
Timestamp when the invitation was resolved.

Null when the invitation is still in pending status. Set to the exact moment the recipient successfully signs up with the matching email address, at which point the invitation is fulfilled and the user is automatically added as an employee of the organization with the assigned role.
resolved_at.x-autobe-specification: Null when the invitation status is 'pending'. Set to the server timestamp at the moment the recipient signs up with the matching email address and the invitation transitions to 'resolved'. Immutable once set.

IErpHrmInvitation.description:
An employee invitation record for joining an organization.

Represents an invitation sent to an email address, inviting that person to join the current organization as an employee. The invitation carries an assigned role that determines the invitee's permissions upon joining.

**Status Lifecycle**: The invitation starts as pending when sent. It transitions to resolved when the recipient signs up with the matching email address, at which point they automatically become an employee with the assigned role.

**Multi-organization**: The same email address can have pending invitations in different organizations simultaneously. Each invitation is scoped to a single organization.
IErpHrmInvitation.x-autobe-specification: Application-layer invitation records with no direct database table mapping. The invitation is constructed by combining the email and role_id from IErpHrmInvitation.ICreate with an organization context from the active member session. The ID is a system-generated UUID v4. Status defaults to 'pending' at creation and transitions to 'resolved' when the recipient signs up with the matching email address, at which point they are automatically added as an employee with the assigned role. The role field is resolved by joining role_id to erp_hrm_roles and returning ISummary. Organization context is implicit from the active session and never exposed in the DTO.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the invitation.

Assigned automatically when the invitation is created and never modified.
id.x-autobe-specification: Primary key of the invitation record. UUID v4 string, auto-generated when the invitation is created. Serves as the unique resource identifier for invitation detail retrieval and resolution operations.

email.description:
The email address of the invited person.

Serves as the matching key for automatic invitation resolution. When someone signs up with this email address, the invitation is automatically resolved and they become an employee of the organization.
email.x-autobe-specification: The email address the invitation was sent to. This is the matching key for automatic invitation resolution per [80]: when a new user signs up with this email address, the system scans for all pending invitations matching it across all organizations and automatically resolves each one, adding the user as an employee to every inviting organization with the role specified at invitation time per [126]. Must be a valid email format. If the email already belongs to an existing user account when the invitation is sent, the user is immediately added as an employee and no invitation record is persisted — so the email here always represents an address not yet registered in the system.

status.description:
Current lifecycle status of the invitation.

Three states exist: pending means the invitation is waiting for the recipient to create an account with the invited email address; fulfilled means the recipient has signed up and been automatically enrolled as an employee in the organization; revoked means the invitation was manually cancelled before the recipient could accept it, permanently terminating the invitation.
status.x-autobe-specification: Lifecycle status of the invitation with three allowed values per the invitation list API operation (PATCH /erpHrm/member/invitations). pending: the invitation has been sent to the email address but the recipient has not yet created an account with that email — the invitation remains open indefinitely awaiting sign-up. fulfilled: the recipient has signed up using the invited email address and has been automatically added to the organization as an employee with the role specified at invitation time. revoked: the invitation was manually cancelled by a user with the employee:manage permission before the recipient could accept it, permanently terminating the invitation. Note: invitations are only created for unknown email addresses per [80]; if the email already belongs to an existing user, the user is immediately added as an employee and no invitation record appears in this collection.

inviter.description:
The employee who sent this invitation.

Contains summary profile information about the inviter, including their name, role, and department within the organization.
inviter.x-autobe-specification: The employee who sent the invitation, surfaced as IErpHrmEmployee.ISummary. Implemented via JOIN: invitation's sender employee ID → erp_hrm_employees table → erp_hrm_members table, providing the inviter's display name, email, role, department, position, employment type, and status. The inviter must have held the employee:manage permission to send the invitation per [126].

created_at.description:
When the invitation was sent.

ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC representing the moment the invitation was created and dispatched to the recipient's email address.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Timestamp when the invitation record was created and sent to the recipient's email address. ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC. Set automatically on creation and never modified after. Used as the default sort key: invitations are listed in descending chronological order so the most recently sent invitations appear first.

IErpHrmInvitation.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of an organization invitation.

Provides a lightweight view of an invitation sent to an external email address to join the organization. Each record displays the invited email address, the current lifecycle status, when the invitation was sent, and who sent it. Used in paginated invitation list responses where each entry provides essential identifying information without the full invitation details.

The status field indicates the invitation's current state: pending for invitations awaiting the recipient's sign-up, and resolved for invitations where the recipient has created an account and been automatically added to the organization as an employee.
IErpHrmInvitation.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Source: invitation records sent to external email addresses for organization enrollment. No single database table loaded — treat as a standalone conceptual entity. Direct fields: id (UUID primary key), email (invited recipient address used for sign-up matching per [80][126]), status (pending — awaiting sign-up; resolved — recipient has signed up and been automatically added to the organization as an employee per [107][113]), created_at (sent timestamp). Relation: inviter composed via JOIN through sender reference to erp_hrm_employees → erp_hrm_members, surfacing as IErpHrmEmployee.ISummary. Excluded from DTO: organization_id (session-scoped), updated_at, deleted_at (filtered at query level), sender FK column, resolved-user reference, HAS-MANY compositions. Sorting: by created_at DESC for most recent invitations first. Note: if the invited email already belongs to an existing user account when the invitation is sent, the user is immediately added as an employee and no invitation record is persisted — only invitations sent to unknown email addresses appear in this collection per [80].

total_budget_hours.description:
Sum of all budget hour estimates across every qualifying project in the report.

Sourced from erp_hrm_projects.budget_hours for all projects matching the filter criteria. Represents the total planned or estimated work hours across the organization's budgeted projects.
total_budget_hours.x-autobe-specification: SUM(erp_hrm_projects.budget_hours) across all projects in the current organization where deleted_at IS NULL AND budget_hours IS NOT NULL. Projects without budget_hours (NULL) are excluded from the sum.

total_actual_hours.description:
Sum of all actual logged hours across every qualifying project in the report.

Computed as the aggregate of per-project actual_hours, derived from SUM(erp_hrm_timelogs.duration_minutes) divided by 60. Includes both billable and non-billable timelogs. Projects with no timelogs contribute zero to this total.
total_actual_hours.x-autobe-specification: SUM(erp_hrm_timelogs.duration_minutes) / 60 across all timelogs whose project_id belongs to a qualifying project in the current organization. Includes both billable and non-billable timelogs. If no timelogs exist for any qualifying project, the total is 0.

overall_utilization.description:

A value above 100% indicates the organization has logged more hours than budgeted across all projects. A value of 0% occurs when there are no qualifying projects (total_budget_hours is zero). This single metric provides a quick organizational health check on project time budget consumption.
